He also conquered the place called Lysias, of which Silas a Jew was tyrant.

dictNote: Lysias, more fully Claudius Lysias, was the Roman tribune who commanded the garrison at the Antonia Fortress in Jerusalem. He rescued Paul from a mob in the temple, had him examined under guard, and later sent him under armed escort to the governor Felix in Caesarea with a letter explaining the case (Acts 21:31-33; 23:26-30). He is not the same person as the Hellenistic-era Syrian regent of the same name mentioned in the books of Maccabees, who lived roughly two centuries earlier.

name: Paphos
dictNote: The capital of the island of Cyprus, and therefore the residence of the Roman governor. It was visited by Paul and Barnabas on their first missionary tour (Acts 13:6). It is new Paphos which is here meant. It lay on the west coast of the island, about 8 miles north of old Paphos. Its modern name is Baffa.

name: Sirion
note: Shirjon or Sirjon, a peak of the Lebanon
dictNote: Sirion was not a person but the Sidonian name for Mount Hermon, the snow-capped peak marking Israel's northern boundary (Deuteronomy 3:9). A psalm pictures Sirion, alongside Lebanon, skipping like a young wild ox at the voice of the Lord in a storm theophany (Psalm 29:6).

name: Galeed
note: Galed, a memorial cairn East of the Jordan
dictNote: Galeed was not a person but the name Jacob gave to a heap of stones he and his father-in-law Laban raised in the hill country to mark a covenant of peace between them (Genesis 31:45-48). Laban called the same pile Jegar-sahadutha in Aramaic, while Jacob's Hebrew name, meaning "heap of witness," gave the surrounding region, Gilead, its lasting name.

name: Jerahmeelites
note: a Jerachmeelite or descendant of Jerachmeel
dictNote: (descendants of Jerahmeel), The, the tribe descended from the first of the foregoing persons. (1 Samuel 27:10) They dwelt in the south of Judah.

name: Hallohesh
dictNote: Hallohesh was one of the leaders who set his seal on the covenant Nehemiah drew up, committing the returned exiles to obey God's law (Nehemiah 10:24). His son or descendant Shallum is also named among those who helped repair Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3:12).

name: Ije-abarim
dictNote: Ruins of Abarim, the forty-seventh station of the Israelites in the wilderness, “in the border of Moab” (Num. 33:44).

name: Beth-anath
dictNote: House of response, one of the fenced cities of Naphtali (Josh. 19:38). It is perhaps identical with the modern village ‘Ainata, 6 miles west of Kedesh.

name: Shual
note: Shual, the name of an Israelite and of a place in Palestine
dictNote: (a jackal), son of Zophah, an Asherite. (1 Chronicles 7:36) (B.C. after 1445.)

name: Iim
note: Ijim, a place in the Desert.
dictNote: Ruins. (1.) A city in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:29). (2.) One of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness (Num. 33:45).

name: Jarha
dictNote: Jarha was an Egyptian servant of Sheshan, a descendant of Judah who had no sons. Sheshan gave Jarha his daughter in marriage to preserve the family line, and their descendants are traced several generations forward in Chronicles, eventually including Zabad, one of David's mighty men (1 Chronicles 2:34-35; 11:41).

name: Zemarite
note: a Tsemarite or branch of the Canaanites
dictNote: The designation of one of the Phoenician tribes (Gen. 10:18) who inhabited the town of Sumra, at the western base of the Lebanon range. In the Amarna tablets (B.C. 1400) Zemar, or Zumur, was one of the most important of the Phoenician cities, but it afterwards almost disappears from history.

name: Abida
note: Abida, a son of Abraham by Keturah
dictNote: Abida was one of five sons of Midian, himself a son Abraham had by his wife Keturah after Sarah's death (Genesis 25:1-4; 1 Chronicles 1:33). He is counted among the ancestors of the Arab tribes that settled east and south of Canaan.

name: Enshemesh
dictNote: (fountain of the sun), a spring which formed one of the landmarks on the north boundary of Judah, (Joshua 15:7) and the south boundary of Benjamin, (Joshua 18:17) perhaps Ain Haud or Ain-Chot—the “well of apostles”—about a mile below Bethany.

name: Mene
dictNote: Mene was not a person but the first word of the mysterious writing that appeared on the wall during Belshazzar's feast in Babylon, which Daniel alone could read and interpret (Daniel 5:25-28). Repeated as "Mene, Mene," it meant "numbered," and Daniel explained it as God's declaration that Belshazzar's kingdom had been measured out and brought to an end; Babylon fell that same night.

name: Peninnah

secondTemple.excerpt: Elcanah, a Levite, one of a middle condition among his fellow citizens; and one that dwelt at Ramathaim, a city of the tribe of Ephraim, married two wives, Hannah and Peninnah.

dictNote: Peninnah was one of Elkanah's two wives and the mother of several children, while his other wife, Hannah, remained childless for years (1 Samuel 1:2). Peninnah taunted Hannah over her barrenness, provoking the grief that led Hannah to pray for a son at Shiloh, a prayer answered with the birth of Samuel (1 Samuel 1:4-7).

name: Hattil
dictNote: Hattil headed a family descended from "Solomon's servants," temple workers whose descendants returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:57; Nehemiah 7:59). Nothing further is recorded about him.

name: Mehida
dictNote: Mehida headed a family of Nethinim, temple servants whose descendants returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:52; Nehemiah 7:54). Nothing further is recorded about him.

name: Tahpenes

secondTemple.excerpt: Egypt, who received him kindly, and assigned him a house to dwell in, and a country to supply him with food; and when he was grown up he loved him exceedingly, insomuch that he gave him his wife's sister, whose name was Tahpenes, to wife, by whom he had a son; who was brought up with the king's children.

dictNote: Tahpenes was an Egyptian queen, the wife of the pharaoh who gave asylum to Hadad the Edomite when he fled Solomon's kingdom. She raised Hadad's son in Pharaoh's own household and gave her sister in marriage to Hadad (1 Kings 11:19-20).

name: Salmon
dictNote: Salmon appears in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus as the father of Boaz by Rahab, the Canaanite woman who sheltered Israel's spies at Jericho (Matthew 1:4-5). He is the same man the book of Ruth calls Salmon or Salma, an ancestor of David through the line that runs from Judah's son Perez down to Jesse (Ruth 4:20-21).

name: Jemuel

secondTemple.excerpt:
Simeon and his sons; and these are the names of his sons: Jemuel, and Jamin, and Ohad,

and Jachin, and Zohar, and Shaul, the son of the Zephathite  woman--seven.

dictNote: Jemuel was the eldest son of Simeon, one of the seventy who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family (Genesis 46:10; Exodus 6:15). He is called Nemuel in the later census list of Simeon's clans (Numbers 26:12).

name: Bazlith
dictNote: Bazlith, also spelled Bazluth, headed a family of Nethinim, temple servants whose descendants returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:52; Nehemiah 7:54). Nothing further is recorded about him.

name: Syene
note: Seven, a place in Upper Egypt
dictNote: Opening (Ezek. 29:10; 30:6), a town of Egypt, on the borders of Ethiopia, now called Assouan, on the right bank of the Nile, notable for its quarries of beautiful red granite called “syenite.” It was the frontier town of Egypt in the south, as Migdol was in the north-east.

name: Kirjathbaal
dictNote: [KIRJATH-JEARIM]

name: Amraphel

secondTemple.excerpt: odomites, who submitted to this slavery twelve years; and so long they continued to pay their tribute: but on the thirteenth year they rebelled; and then the army of the Assyrians came upon them, under their commanders, Amraphel , Arioch , Chodorlaomor , and Tidal .

And in this year came Chedorlaomer, king of Elam, and Amraphel, king of Shinar, and Arioch, king of Sêllâsar  and Têrgâl,  king of nations, and slew the king of Gomorrah, and the king of Sodom fled, and many fell through wounds in the vale of Siddim, by the Salt Sea.

dictNote: Amraphel was the king of Shinar, in southern Mesopotamia, who joined Chedorlaomer of Elam and two other kings in a campaign against the cities of the plain, including Sodom, described in Genesis 14. Older scholarship once proposed identifying him with the famous Babylonian king Hammurabi, whose law code survives on a well-known stone stele, but most scholars today consider the equation linguistically and chronologically doubtful.

name: Epaphroditus
dictNote: Epaphroditus was a member of the church at Philippi whom the congregation sent to Rome carrying financial support for the imprisoned Paul. He fell seriously ill while there, and Paul, moved by his recovery and homesickness, sent him back to Philippi bearing the letter now known as Philippians, commending him warmly to the church (Philippians 2:25-30; 4:18).

name: Kishion
dictNote: Hardness, a city of Issachar assigned to the Gershonite Levites (Josh. 19:20), the same as Kishon (21:28).

name: Hauran
note: Chavran, a region East of the Jordan
dictNote: Cave-land, mentioned only in Ezek. 47:16, 18. It was one of the ancient divisions of Bashan (q.v.), and lay on the south-east of Gaulanitis or the Jaulan, and on the south of Lejah, extending from the Arnon to the Hieromax. It was the most fertile region in Syria, and to this day abounds in the ruins of towns, many of which have stone doors and massive walls. It retains its ancient name. It was known by the Greeks and Romans as “Auranitis.”

name: Tartan

secondTemple.excerpt:
The names of the two other commanders were Tartan and Rabsaris.

dictNote: Tartan was not a personal name but an Assyrian military title meaning roughly "commander-in-chief." One tartan served as one of Sennacherib's envoys sent to demand Jerusalem's surrender under Hezekiah (2 Kings 18:17). An earlier tartan led Sargon II's campaign against Ashdod, an operation Sargon's own palace inscriptions at Khorsabad independently record (Isaiah 20:1).

name: Onesimus
dictNote: Onesimus was a runaway slave who ended up with Paul during one of Paul's imprisonments and became a Christian there, and Paul sent him back to his owner Philemon along with a personal letter, tactfully asking Philemon to receive Onesimus back not as a slave but as a beloved brother.

name: Aeneas

dictNote: Aeneas was a paralyzed man at Lydda who had been bedridden for eight years before Peter healed him, telling him to get up and make his bed; the miracle led many in Lydda and the nearby plain of Sharon to turn to the Lord (Acts 9:32-35).

name: Sophereth
dictNote: Sophereth headed a family descended from "Solomon's servants," temple workers whose descendants returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:55; Nehemiah 7:57). Nothing further is recorded about him.

name: Mattanah
note: Mattanah, a place in the Desert
dictNote: A gift, a station of the Israelites (Num. 21:18, 19) between the desert and the borders of Moab, in the Wady Waleh.

name: Ahiam
dictNote: Ahiam, son of Sharar (also called Sacar) the Hararite, was one of David's thirty mighty warriors (2 Samuel 23:33; 1 Chronicles 11:35). Nothing further is recorded about him.

name: Baal-berith
note: Baal-Berith, a special deity of the Shechemites
dictNote: Baal-berith, meaning "lord of the covenant," was not a person but a Canaanite god worshipped at Shechem after Gideon's death, when Israel again fell into idolatry (Judges 8:33). The same shrine is later called simply the house of the god "El-berith" or "Berith," and it funded the violent bid for kingship by Gideon's son Abimelech (Judges 9:4, 46).

name: Col-hozeh
dictNote: Col-hozeh was a man of the tribe of Judah whose son Shallun repaired the Fountain Gate and part of Jerusalem's wall during Nehemiah's rebuilding project (Nehemiah 3:15). A descendant, Baruch, is also listed among Jerusalem's returned residents (Nehemiah 11:5).

Paul later calls a Lucius his kinsman in his greetings from Corinth, though it is uncertain whether this is the same man (Romans 16:21).

name: Ishvah

secondTemple.excerpt: And the sons of Asher: Imnah, and Ishvah, (and Ishvi), and Beriah, and Serah, their one sister--six.

dictNote: Ishvah was a son of Asher who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family (Genesis 46:17; 1 Chronicles 7:30). He is absent from the later clan census of Asher in Numbers 26, which may mean he died without founding a family line.

name: Ellasar
note: Ellasar, an early country of Asia
dictNote: Ellasar was not a person but the kingdom ruled by Arioch, one of the four kings who campaigned against Sodom and its allies alongside Chedorlaomer of Elam (Genesis 14:1, 9). Many scholars connect it with Larsa, an ancient Mesopotamian city between Ur and Uruk that has been extensively excavated and whose ruins preserve royal inscriptions from its own line of kings.

name: Madmannah
dictNote: Dunghill, the modern el-Minyay, 15 miles south-south-west of Gaza (Josh. 15:31; 1 Chr. 2:49), in the south of Judah. The Pal. Mem., however, suggest Umm Deimneh, 12 miles north-east of Beersheba, as the site.

name: Hashabniah
note: Chashabnejah, the name of two Israelites
dictNote: Hashabniah was the name of two men in Nehemiah's time. One was the father of Hattush, who helped repair Jerusalem's wall (Nehemiah 3:10). The other was a Levite who joined in leading Israel's public confession and prayer after the wall's completion (Nehemiah 9:4-5).

name: Sheshach
note: Sheshak, a symbolic name of Babylon
dictNote: Sheshach was not a person but a coded name for Babylon, formed by substituting each Hebrew letter with its counterpart counted from the opposite end of the alphabet, a cipher called atbash. Jeremiah used the name in oracles against Babylon, and its parallel with "Babylon" in the surrounding verses confirms the identification (Jeremiah 25:26; 51:41).

name: Gethsemane
note: oil-press; Gethsemane, a garden near Jerusalem
dictNote: Gethsemane was not a person but an olive grove at the foot of the Mount of Olives, just across the Kidron Valley from Jerusalem, where Jesus often withdrew with his disciples and where he agonized in prayer the night he was betrayed and arrested (Matthew 26:36-46; John 18:1-2). The garden has been venerated at roughly this location since at least the fourth century, though the olive trees standing there today have been radiocarbon-dated to the medieval period rather than to the first century.

name: Hor-hagidgad
note: Chor-hag-Gidgad, a place in the Desert
dictNote: (conspicous mountain), the name of the desert station where the Israelites encamped, (Numbers 33:32) probably the same as Gudgodah. (10:7)

name: Ekronite
note: an Ekronite or inhabitant of Ekron

name: Habaiah
dictNote: Habaiah headed a priestly family that returned from Babylonian exile but could not produce genealogical records proving descent from Aaron. As a result its members were barred from serving as priests and from eating the priests' portion of offerings until the matter could be settled by the high priest using the Urim and Thummim, a resolution the record does not describe as ever occurring (Ezra 2:61-63; Nehemiah 7:63-65).

name: Tertullus
dictNote: Tertullus was a professional orator hired by the Jewish leadership to present their accusations against Paul before the Roman governor Felix in Caesarea. He flattered Felix at length before charging Paul with stirring up unrest, leading the sect of the Nazarenes, and attempting to profane the temple (Acts 24:1-9).

name: Padon
dictNote: Padon headed a family of Nethinim, temple servants whose descendants returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:44; Nehemiah 7:47). Nothing further is recorded about him.

name: Zabdiel
note: gift of God; Zabdiel, the name of two Israelites
dictNote: Zabdiel was the name of two men. One was the father of Jashobeam, a chief officer in David's army (1 Chronicles 27:2). The other oversaw 128 valiant men engaged in temple-related work in Jerusalem after the exile (Nehemiah 11:14).

name: Romamti-ezer
dictNote: Romamti-ezer was a son of Heman, David's seer, and was set apart along with his brothers for the ministry of music in the temple. He headed the twenty-fourth of the twenty-four courses assigned to lead worship by casting lots (1 Chronicles 25:4, 31).

name: Sheariah
dictNote: Sheariah was a descendant of Saul through Jonathan's son Merib-baal, part of the genealogy Chronicles preserves for Saul's line after the family's near destruction (1 Chronicles 8:38; 9:44). Nothing further is recorded about him.

name: Zelek
dictNote: Zelek was an Ammonite who served among David's thirty mighty warriors, an unusual inclusion of a foreigner among David's elite fighting men (2 Samuel 23:37; 1 Chronicles 11:39).

name: Tiras

secondTemple.excerpt: The sons of Japheth: Gomer and Magog and Madai and Javan, Tubal and Meshech and Tiras: these are 1324-1372 A.M.

And for Tiras  there came forth the seventh portion, four great islands  in the midst of the sea, which reach to the portion of Ham [and the islands of Kamâtûrî came out by lot for the sons of Arpachshad as his inheritance].  14.

dictNote: Tiras was the youngest son of Japheth, listed in the Table of Nations as the ancestor of a people group whose location Genesis does not specify (Genesis 10:2; 1 Chronicles 1:5). Later Jewish tradition, recorded by Josephus, associated his descendants with the Thracians, though the identification cannot be confirmed.

name: Shamgar

secondTemple.excerpt: After him Shamgar, the son of Anath, was elected for their governour; but died in the first year of his government.

dictNote: Shamgar, son of Anath, delivered Israel from a Philistine incursion by killing six hundred men with an ox goad, a long, sharp-tipped pole used for driving cattle (Judges 3:31). He is remembered again in the Song of Deborah as a figure from a dangerous era when travel on the main roads had become unsafe (Judges 5:6).

name: Jerah
dictNote: Jerah was a son of Joktan, in the line of Shem, and the ancestor of one of the Arabian tribes descended from him (Genesis 10:26; 1 Chronicles 1:20). His name means "moon" in Hebrew, though little else is known about the tribe he represents.

name: Abia
note: Abijah, the name of two Israelites

secondTemple.excerpt: Accordingly they wrote to Abia, King of the Arabians; and promised him great sums of money, if he would make an expedition against their King: and they farther promised him, that, on the first onset, they would desert their King; because they were de

dictNote: Abia is the Greek form of the Hebrew name Abijah. Matthew's genealogy of Jesus uses it for Abijah, king of Judah and son of Rehoboam (Matthew 1:7). Luke uses it differently, naming the eighth of the twenty-four priestly divisions David established, the division to which Zechariah, father of John the Baptist, belonged (Luke 1:5; 1 Chronicles 24:10).

name: Hashupha
dictNote: Hashupha, also spelled Hasupha, headed a family of Nethinim, temple servants whose descendants returned from Babylonian exile in the first group led by Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:43; Nehemiah 7:46). Nothing further is recorded about him.

name: Abishur
dictNote: Abishur was a descendant of Judah listed in the genealogy of Jerahmeel's family, one of two sons of Shammai (1 Chronicles 2:28-29). Nothing else is recorded about him beyond his place in this list of clan heads.

name: Melech
note: Melek, the name of two Israelites
dictNote: Melech was a great-grandson of Jonathan through his father Micah and grandfather Mephibosheth, listed among the descendants of Saul's house in the tribe of Benjamin (1 Chronicles 8:35; 9:41). He appears only in this genealogical record.

name: Tel-melah
dictNote: Hill of salt, a place in Babylon from which the Jews returned (id.).

name: Anamim
note: Anamim, a son of Mizraim and his descendants, with their country
dictNote: Anamim was not an individual but one of the tribal groups descended from Mizraim, the biblical name for Egypt, in the Table of Nations (Genesis 10:13; 1 Chronicles 1:11). Like several names in this list, its exact historical people group has not been identified with confidence, though scholars have proposed connections to various Egyptian or Libyan populations.

name: Shashak
dictNote: Shashak was a Benjamite listed among the sons of Beriah in the tribal genealogy of 1 Chronicles 8:14 and 25. He is mentioned only in this record of Benjamin's clans.

name: Elishua
note: Elishua, the son of King David
dictNote: Elishua was one of David's sons born to him in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:15). The parallel genealogy in 1 Chronicles 3:6 lists the same son under the name Elishama.

name: Barsabas
note: son of Sabas (or Tsaba); Bar-sabas, the name of two Israelites
dictNote: Barsabas, meaning son of Sabas, was a surname carried by two different men in Acts. Joseph Barsabas, also called Justus, was one of the two candidates put forward to replace Judas among the twelve apostles (Acts 1:23). Judas Barsabas was a prophet in the Jerusalem church sent along with Paul and Silas to deliver the council's letter to the believers in Antioch (Acts 15:22, 32). The two are unrelated beyond sharing the same family name.

name: Melzar
note: the butler or other officer in the Babylonian court
dictNote: Melzar is not a personal name but the title of a Babylonian court official, roughly a steward or chief attendant, who was placed in charge of the diet of Daniel and his three companions (Daniel 1:11, 16). The Hebrew term functions more like an office than an individual's name, which is why some translations render it as 'the guard' or 'the steward' rather than treating it as a proper noun.

name: Ibzan

secondTemple.excerpt: 1195] Now when Jephtha was dead, Ibzan took the government; being of the tribe of Judah, and of the city of Bethlehem.

dictNote: Ibzan was the tenth judge of Israel, ruling for seven years from his hometown of Bethlehem (Judges 12:8-10). The text notes that he had thirty sons and thirty daughters, but records nothing else of his rule.

name: Shalmai
dictNote: Shalmai was the ancestral head of a family among the Nethinim, the temple servants whose descendants returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:46). The parallel list in Nehemiah 7:48 gives the name as Salmai.

name: Bethmarcaboth
note: Beth-ham-Markaboth or Beth-Markaboth, a place in Palestine
dictNote: (house of the chariots), one of the towns of Simeon, situated to the extreme south of Judah. (Joshua 19:5; 1 Chronicles 4:31) In the parallel list, (Joshua 15:31) Madmannah occurs in place of Beth-marcaboth.

name: Mallothi
dictNote: Mallothi was a Levite musician, one of the sons of Heman appointed by David to the temple music service (1 Chronicles 25:4). He headed the nineteenth of the twenty-four divisions of musicians chosen by lot (25:26).

name: Nisroch
dictNote: Nisroch was not a person but a god in the Assyrian pantheon, worshiped with the head of an eagle, in whose temple King Sennacherib of Assyria was assassinated by his own sons (2 Kings 19:37; Isaiah 37:38). The god's name does not correspond cleanly to any deity known from surviving Assyrian records, and it may be a scribal corruption of another god's name such as Nusku. Sennacherib's murder itself is corroborated outside the Bible: the Babylonian Chronicle and later Assyrian records confirm he was killed by one of his own sons in a palace coup.

name: Darkon
dictNote: Darkon was the ancestral head of a family among the 'servants of Solomon,' a class of temple workers, whose descendants returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel (Ezra 2:56; Nehemiah 7:58).

name: Eshban
dictNote: Eshban was a Horite, one of the four sons of Dishon listed among the clan chiefs of Seir in Edom's genealogy (Genesis 36:26; 1 Chronicles 1:41).

name: Pinon
dictNote: Pinon appears among the chiefs, or 'dukes,' of Edom in the genealogical lists of Genesis 36:41 and 1 Chronicles 1:52, where each name marks the head of a clan or territory. Many scholars think Pinon is the same as Punon, an Edomite way station named in Numbers 33:42-43, associated with the copper mining region of Feinan in the Jordan valley, where archaeologists have uncovered extensive ancient smelting sites.

name: Jehoiarib
note: Jehojarib, the name of two Israelites
dictNote: Jehoiarib was a priest in Jerusalem who headed the first of the twenty-four priestly divisions organized for temple service (1 Chronicles 9:10; 24:7). His course continued after the Babylonian exile, and the priestly family of Mattathias and his sons, the Maccabees, later traced its descent from this division.

name: Lemuel
note: Lemuel or Lemoel, a symbolic name of Solomon
dictNote: Lemuel was a king whose mother's wise instruction is recorded in Proverbs 31:1-9, advice about avoiding wine and defending the poor and needy. Nothing certain is known about which kingdom he ruled, and later Jewish tradition sometimes identified him with Solomon under a symbolic name, though this cannot be confirmed.

dictNote: The country between the two rivers (Heb. Aram-naharaim; i.e., “Syria of the two rivers”), the name given by the Greeks and Romans to the region between the Euphrates and the Tigris (Gen. 24:10; Deut. 23:4; Judg. 3:8, 10). In the Old Testament it is mentioned also under the name “Padan-aram;” i.e., the plain of Aram, or Syria (Gen. 25:20). The northern portion of this fertile plateau was the original home of the ancestors of the Hebrews (Gen. 11; Acts 7:2). From this region Isaac obtained his wife Rebecca (Gen. 24:10, 15), and here also Jacob sojourned (28:2-7) and obtained his wives, and here most of his sons were born (35:26; 46:15). The petty, independent tribes of this region, each under its own prince, were warlike, and used chariots in battle. They maintained their independence till after the time of David, when they fell under the dominion of Assyria, and were absorbed into the empire (2 Kings 19:13).

name: Abda
note: Abda, the name of two Israelites
dictNote: Abda is the name of two Old Testament men. The first was the father of Adoniram, whom Solomon put in charge of the forced labor levy (1 Kings 4:6). The second was a Levite of the family of Jeduthun who lived in Jerusalem after the exile (Nehemiah 11:17); the parallel list in 1 Chronicles 9:16 calls this same man Obadiah.

name: Areopagus
note: rock of Ares, a place in Athens
dictNote: The Latin form of the Greek word rendered “Mars’ hill.” But it denotes also the council or court of justice which met in the open air on the hill. It was a rocky height to the west of the Acropolis at Athens, on the south-east summit of which the council was held which was constituted by Solon, and consisted of nine archons or chief magistrates who were then in office, and the ex-archons of blameless life. On this hill of Mars (Gr. Ares) Paul delivered his memorable address to the “men of Athens” (Acts 17:22-31).

name: Noadiah
note: Noadjah, the name of an Israelite, and a false prophetess
dictNote: Noadiah is the name of two different figures. One was a Levite who returned from Babylon with Ezra and helped weigh out the temple treasures (Ezra 8:33). The other was a prophetess who, together with the enemies Tobiah and Sanballat, tried to intimidate and discourage Nehemiah while he was rebuilding Jerusalem's walls (Nehemiah 6:14).

name: Barachel
note: Barakel, the father of one of Job's friends
dictNote: Barachel was a Buzite, the father of Elihu, the youngest of the friends who spoke to Job (Job 32:2, 6).

name: Crispus
dictNote: Crispus was the leader of the Jewish synagogue in Corinth who came to believe in Christ under Paul's preaching there (Acts 18:8). Paul later recalled personally baptizing him, one of the few Corinthian converts Paul baptized himself (1 Corinthians 1:14).

name: Shephi
dictNote: Shephi was a son of Shobal descended from Seir the Horite, listed among Edom's clan chiefs (1 Chronicles 1:40). The parallel genealogy in Genesis 36:23 gives his name as Shepho.

name: Jogbehah
note: Jogbehah, a place East of the Jordan
dictNote: (lofty), one of the cities on the east of Jordan which were built and fortified by the tribe of Gad when they took possession of their territory. (Numbers 32:35)

name: Almodad
dictNote: Almodad was the first named of the sons of Joktan in the Table of Nations, understood as the ancestor of an Arabian tribe (Genesis 10:26; 1 Chronicles 1:20). His descendants are usually placed somewhere in the Arabian peninsula, though the exact tribe has not been identified with certainty.

name: Eri

secondTemple.excerpt: And these are the names of their sons who went with him into Egypt: the sons of Gad: Ziphion, and Haggi, and Shuni, and Ezbon, (and Eri) and Areli, and Arodi--eight.

dictNote: Eri was a son of Gad who went down to Egypt with Jacob's family, and his descendants became the clan of the Erites counted in the wilderness census (Genesis 46:16; Numbers 26:16).

name: Sabtecha
note: Sabteca, the name of a son of Cush, and the region settled by him
dictNote: The fifth son of Cush (id.).

name: Ezekiel
note: The priest-prophet exiled to Babylon whose visions open with the famous wheels-within-wheels (Ezekiel 1:3). Josephus mentions him more briefly than Jeremiah here — the honest gap in this particular chapter — but places him exactly where Scripture does: warning King Zedekiah, unheeded, right before the final fall of Jerusalem.

secondTemple.excerpt: This King would not believe what was predicted by Jeremiah and Ezekiel.

dictNote: Ezekiel was a priest deported to Babylon in the first wave of exiles who began prophesying five years into his captivity after a vision of God's throne, described in famously strange imagery of wheels within wheels and four living creatures. He acted out many of his prophecies physically, lying on his side for over a year to symbolize the years of Israel's sin, and his most famous vision is a valley of dry bones brought back to life, a picture of national restoration after exile.

name: Migdal-el
dictNote: Tower of God, a fortified city of Naphtali (Josh. 19:38), supposed by some to be identical with Magdala (q.v.).

name: Maath
dictNote: Maath appears only as a name in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, listed among the ancestors between the exile and Joseph (Luke 3:26). Nothing else is known about him.

name: Saruch
dictNote: Saruch is the Greek form, used in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, of the Old Testament name Serug, the son of Reu and an ancestor of Abraham (Luke 3:35; compare Genesis 11:20-23).

name: Azaniah
dictNote: Azaniah was a Levite, the father of Jeshua, one of the Levites who set their seal to the covenant renewed under Nehemiah after the exile (Nehemiah 10:9).

name: Nachor
dictNote: Nachor is the Greek form, used in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, of the Old Testament name Nahor, grandfather of Abraham (Luke 3:34; compare Genesis 11:24-26).

name: Letushim
dictNote: Letushim was not an individual but one of three tribal groups, alongside Asshurim and Leummim, descended from Dedan, a grandson of Abraham through Keturah (Genesis 25:3). Like the other two, its plural Hebrew form marks it as the name of a clan or people rather than a single ancestor, and its historical identity is uncertain.

name: Jokim
dictNote: Jokim was a descendant of Shelah, the son of Judah, listed in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles 4:22.

name: Ishpan
dictNote: Ishpan was a Benjamite listed among the family of Shashak in the tribal genealogy of 1 Chronicles 8:22.

name: Zethan
dictNote: Zethan was a Benjamite named in the tribal genealogy of 1 Chronicles 7:10.

name: Paltite
note: a Paltite or descendant of Palti
dictNote: The designation of one of David’s heroes (2 Sam. 23:26); called also the Pelonite (1 Chr. 11:27).

name: Zaphnath-paaneah
dictNote: Zaphnath-paaneah is not a separate person but the Egyptian title or name Pharaoh gave to Joseph when he made him governor over Egypt (Genesis 41:45). The name is genuinely Egyptian, though scholars disagree on its exact meaning, with proposals ranging from 'God speaks and he lives' to a title connected to Joseph's administrative role.

name: Jaakobah
dictNote: Jaakobah, a name built from the same root as Jacob, was a descendant of Simeon listed among the clan leaders of that tribe (1 Chronicles 4:36).

name: Hukkok
note: Chukkok or Chukok, a place in Palestine
dictNote: Decreed, a town near Zebulun, not far from Jordan, on the border of Naphtali (Josh. 19:34). (See HELKATH.)

name: Maralah
dictNote: Trembling, a place on the southern boundary of Zebulun (Josh. 19:11). It has been identified with the modern M’alul, about 4 miles south-west of Nazareth.

name: Cleopas
dictNote: Cleopas was one of two disciples whom the risen Jesus joined on the road to Emmaus, not recognizing him until he broke bread with them (Luke 24:13-18, 30-31). Some have identified him with the Clopas mentioned in John 19:25 as the husband of one of the women at the cross, but this cannot be confirmed.

name: Junias
dictNote: Junias, or Junia, is a name Paul greets alongside Andronicus in Romans 16:7, calling the pair his relatives and fellow prisoners who were 'outstanding among the apostles.' Whether the Greek name is the masculine Junias or the far more common feminine Junia has been debated, and most modern scholars now favor Junia, which would make her a woman recognized in the earliest church in a role connected to the apostles.

name: Zara
dictNote: Zara is the form used in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus (Matthew 1:3) for Zerah, the twin brother of Perez born to Judah and Tamar (Genesis 38:27-30). Matthew lists him only to mark the line continuing through his brother Perez, since Zerah himself is not an ancestor of Jesus.

name: Pharpar
dictNote: Swift, one of the rivers of Damascus (2 Kings 5:12). It has been identified with the ‘Awaj, “a small lively river.” The whole of the district watered by the ‘Awaj is called the Wady el-‘Ajam, i.e., “the valley of the Persians”, so called for some unknown reason. This river empties itself into the lake or marsh Bahret Hijaneh, on the east of Damascus. One of its branches bears the modern name of Wady Barbar, which is probably a corruption of Pharpar.

name: Shethar
dictNote: Shethar was one of the seven princes of Media and Persia who had access to King Ahasuerus and advised him at the start of the book of Esther (Esther 1:14).

name: Asareel
dictNote: Asareel was a son of Jehaleleel listed in the genealogies of the tribe of Judah (1 Chronicles 4:16).

name: Izrahite
note: a Jizrach (i.e. Ezrachite or Zarchite) or descendant of Zerach
dictNote: The designation of one of David’s officers (1 Chr. 27:8).

name: Gimzo
dictNote: A place fertile in sycamores, a city in the plain of Judah, the villages of which were seized by the Philistines (2 Chr. 28:18). It is now called Jimzu, about 3 miles south-east of Ludd, i.e., Lydda.

name: Betonim
dictNote: a town of Gad, apparently on the northern boundary. (Joshua 13:26)

name: Olympas
dictNote: Olympas was a Christian in Rome whom Paul greets by name at the close of his letter to the Romans (Romans 16:15). Nothing further is known about him.

name: Aven
note: Aven, the contemptuous synonym of three places, one in Coele-Syria, one in Egypt (On), and one in Palestine (Bethel)
dictNote: Aven is not a person but a Hebrew word meaning nothingness or vanity, used in several places as a mocking wordplay on real place names. Hosea applies it to Bethel, calling it Beth-aven, 'house of vanity,' because of the golden calf Jeroboam had set up there (Hosea 4:15; 10:8). Ezekiel 30:17 uses it for the Egyptian city of On, better known as Heliopolis, and Amos 1:5 uses it for a Syrian city usually identified with Baalbec.

name: Elon-bethhanan
note: Elon of Beth-chanan, a place in Palestine
dictNote: (oak of the house of grace) is named with two Danite towns as forming one of Solomon’s commissariat districts. (1 Kings 4:9)

name: Roboam
dictNote: Roboam is the Greek form, used in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus, of Rehoboam, Solomon's son who succeeded him as king and under whom the kingdom split in two (Matthew 1:7; compare 1 Kings 12).

name: Sarepta
note: Sarepta (i.e. Tsarephath), a place in Palestine

name: Appii
note: (in the genitive, i.e. possessive case) of Appius, the name of a Roman
dictNote: Appii, more fully 'Appii Forum' in most English Bibles, is not a person but a town or market square along the Appian Way in Italy, about 43 miles from Rome, where a group of Christians met Paul as he traveled toward the capital as a prisoner (Acts 28:15).

name: Beth-aram
note: Beth-ha-Ram, a place East of the Jordan
dictNote: House of the height; i.e., “mountain-house”, one of the towns of Gad, 3 miles east of Jordan, opposite Jericho (Josh. 13:27). Probably the same as Beth-haran in Num. 32:36. It was called by king Herod, Julias, or Livias, after Livia, the wife of Augustus. It is now called Beit-haran.

name: Besodeiah
dictNote: Besodeiah was the father of one of the men who repaired the old gate of Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah (Nehemiah 3:6).

name: Raphu
dictNote: Raphu was a Benjamite, the father of Palti, one of the twelve spies Moses sent to scout the land of Canaan (Numbers 13:9).

name: Dalphon
dictNote: Dalphon was the second named of Haman's ten sons, all of whom were killed by the Jews of Susa after Haman's plot against them failed and were afterward hanged on gallows (Esther 9:7-10).

name: Shadrach
note: Shadrak, the Babylonian name of one of Daniel's companions

secondTemple.excerpt: Daniel he called Baltasar: Ananias, Shadrach: Misael, Meshach: and Azarias, Abednego.

dictNote: Shadrach was the Babylonian name given to Hananiah, one of the young Judean nobles taken captive to Babylon with Daniel (Daniel 1:6-7). Along with his companions Meshach and Abednego, he refused to bow to Nebuchadnezzar's golden image and was thrown into a furnace, from which the three emerged unharmed (Daniel 3:12-30).

name: Eunice
dictNote: Eunice was the mother of Timothy, a Jewish believer married to a Greek man (Acts 16:1). Paul commends her sincere faith and credits her, along with Timothy's grandmother Lois, with raising him in the Scriptures from childhood (2 Timothy 1:5; 3:15).

name: Malchiram
dictNote: Malchiram was a son of King Jeconiah, also called Jehoiachin, born during or after the family's Babylonian captivity (1 Chronicles 3:18).

name: Maadai
dictNote: Maadai was one of the Israelites listed in Ezra 10:34 among those who had married foreign wives after the return from exile and agreed to separate from them as part of Ezra's reform.

dictNote: Myrrh, an ancient city of Ionia, on the western coast of Asia Minor, about 40 miles to the north of Ephesus. It is now the chief city of Anatolia, having a mixed population of about 200,000, of whom about one-third are professed Christians. The church founded here was one of the seven addressed by our Lord (Rev. 2:8-11). The celebrated Polycarp, a pupil of the apostle John, was in the second century a prominent leader in the church of Smyrna. Here he suffered martyrdom, A.D. 155.

dictNote: Moses was born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's own household, only to flee into the desert after killing an Egyptian overseer and spend the next forty years as a shepherd in Midian. God called him back through the burning bush to confront Pharaoh and lead Israel out of slavery, and Moses spent the rest of his life shaping that liberated people into a nation, delivering the law at Sinai and leading them through forty years in the wilderness before dying within sight of the promised land at a hundred and twenty. He is named more often than anyone else in the Old Testament, and archaeology confirms plenty of the world he moved through, the store cities, the Egyptian court, the route through Sinai, without ever turning up a record of Moses himself.

name: Candace
dictNote: A hereditary title, not a personal name, carried by the ruling queens of the Kushite kingdom centered at Meroe in Nubia, comparable to "Pharaoh" for Egypt's kings. The treasury official of one such queen was converted and baptized by Philip on the road from Jerusalem to Gaza (Acts 8:27). The power of these Kushite queens is corroborated outside the Bible: Roman sources describe a war between Rome and a Kushite army led by one of them around 24 BC, and archaeologists later recovered a bronze head of Augustus that Kushite forces had looted and buried beneath the steps of a Meroe temple as an act of triumph, now held in the British Museum.

name: Shiloah
dictNote: The "waters of Shiloah," a gently flowing channel carrying water from the Gihon spring into Jerusalem, later linked with the pool of Siloam (Isaiah 8:6). Isaiah contrasts its quiet flow with the overwhelming flood of the Euphrates as an image of trusting God rather than seeking help from Assyria. The city's ancient water system that this name refers to is documented archaeologically by Hezekiah's Siloam Tunnel and the Hebrew inscription its diggers left inside it, discovered in 1880.

dictNote: Middle district, Vulgate, Messa. (1.) A plain in that part of the boundaries of Arabia inhabited by the descendants of Joktan (Gen. 10:30). (2.) Heb. meysh’a, “deliverance,” the eldest son of Caleb (1 Chr. 2:42), and brother of Jerahmeel. (3.) Heb. id, a king of Moab, the son of Chemosh-Gad, a man of great wealth in flocks and herds (2 Kings 3:4). After the death of Ahab at Ramoth-Gilead, Mesha shook off the yoke of Israel; but on the ascension of Jehoram to the throne of Israel, that king sought the help of Jehoshaphat in an attempt to reduce the Moabites again to their former condition. The united armies of the two kings came unexpectedly on the army of the Moabites, and gained over them an easy victory. The whole land was devastated by the conquering armies, and Mesha sought refuge in his last stronghold, Kir-harasheth (q.v.). Reduced to despair, he ascended the wall of the city, and there, in the sight of the allied armies, offered his first-born son a sacrifice to Chemosh, the fire-god of the Moabites. This fearful spectacle filled the beholders with horror, and they retired from before the besieged city, and recrossed the Jordan laden with spoil (2 Kings 3:25-27). The exploits of Mesha are recorded in the Phoenician inscription on a block of black basalt found at Dibon, in Moab, usually called the “Moabite stone” (q.v.).

name: Tophet
dictNote: =Topheth, from Heb. toph “a drum,” because the cries of children here sacrificed by the priests of Moloch were drowned by the noise of such an instrument; or from taph or toph, meaning “to burn,” and hence a place of burning, the name of a particular part in the valley of Hinnom. “Fire being the most destructive of all elements, is chosen by the sacred writers to symbolize the agency by which God punishes or destroys the wicked. We are not to assume from prophetical figures that material fire is the precise agent to be used. It was not the agency employed in the destruction of Sennacherib, mentioned in Isa. 30:33...Tophet properly begins where the Vale of Hinnom bends round to the east, having the cliffs of Zion on the north, and the Hill of Evil Counsel on the south. It terminates at Beer ‘Ayub, where it joins the Valley of Jehoshaphat. The cliffs on the southern side especially abound in ancient tombs. Here the dead carcasses of beasts and every offal and abomination were cast, and left to be either devoured by that worm that never died or consumed by that fire that was never quenched.” Thus Tophet came to represent the place of punishment. name: Mosera
note: Moserah, a place in the Desert
dictNote: A bond, one of the stations of the Israelites in the wilderness (Deut. 10:6), at the foot of Mount Hor. (Comp. Num. 33:37, 38). It has been identified with el-Tayibeh, a small fountain at the bottom of the pass leading to the ascent of Mount Hor.

name: Elkoshite
note: an Elkoshite or native of Elkosh

name: Malchielite
note: a Malkielite or descendant of Malkiel

name: Hazo
dictNote: One of the sons of Nahor, Abraham's brother, by his wife Milcah, listed among the Aramean clans descended from him (Genesis 22:22).

name: Rachal
dictNote: Traffic, a town in the tribe of Judah, to which David sent presents from the spoils of his enemies (1 Sam. 30:29).

name: Urbanus
dictNote: the form given in the Revised Version for Urbane.

name: Elul

dictNote: Elul is not a person but the sixth month of the Hebrew religious calendar and twelfth of the civil calendar, falling in August and September. Nehemiah completed Jerusalem's wall on the twenty-fifth day of Elul, a project that took fifty-two days (Nehemiah 6:15).

name: Janum (from the margin)
dictNote: Slumber, a town in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:53).

name: Anim
dictNote: Fountains, a city in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:50), now el-Ghuwein, near Eshtemoh, about 10 miles south-west of Hebron.

name: Idalah
dictNote: Snares(?), a city near the west border of Zebulun (Josh. 19:15). It has been identified with the modern Jeida, in the valley of Kishon.

name: Ramath-lehi
dictNote: Elevation of Lehi, or the jawbone height; i.e., the Ramah of Lehi (Judg. 15:15-17). The phrase “in the jaw,” ver. 19, Authorized Version, is in the margin, also in the Revised Version, “in Lehi.” Here Samson slew a thousand Philistines with a jawbone.

name: Salmon
dictNote: Son of Nahshon, the leader of Judah's tribe under Moses, Salmon married Rahab of Jericho and became the father of Boaz, placing him in the ancestral line of David and, through Matthew's genealogy, of Jesus (Ruth 4:20-21; Matthew 1:4-5). He also appears as Salma in the fuller Chronicles genealogy of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:11, 51).

name: Cabbon
dictNote: a town in the low country of Judah. (Joshua 15:40)

name: Jaasau
dictNote: One of the Israelites listed in Ezra's record who agreed to separate from the foreign wives they had married during the years Israelites lived among the surrounding nations (Ezra 10:37).

name: Nehushtan
note: something made of copper, i.e. the copper serpent of the Desert
dictNote: Nehushtan is the contemptuous name King Hezekiah gave to the bronze serpent Moses had made in the wilderness to heal those bitten by venomous snakes (Numbers 21:8-9). Over the centuries Israelites had begun burning incense to the relic as an idol, so Hezekiah destroyed it as part of his religious reforms, dismissing it as “a mere piece of bronze” (2 Kings 18:4).

name: Haggiah
dictNote: A Levite of the Merarite clan, listed in the genealogy of Levi's descendants who served in the temple (1 Chronicles 6:30).

name: Tabbath
note: Tabbath, a place East of the Jordan
dictNote: Famous, a town in the tribe of Ephraim (Judg. 7:22), to the south of Bethshean, near the Jordan.

name: Tizite
note: a Titsite or descendant or inhabitant of an unknown Tits

name: Beth-ezel
dictNote: (neighbor’s house), a place named only in (Micah 1:11) From the context it was doubtless situated in the plain of Philistia.

name: Hazar-addar
dictNote: Village of Addar, a place in the southern boundary of Palestine (Num. 34:4), in the desert to the west of Kadesh-barnea. It is called Adar in Josh. 15:3.

name: Helem
note: Helem, the name of two Israelites
dictNote: A descendant of Asher, listed in the tribal genealogy as a great-grandson through the line of Beriah (1 Chronicles 7:35).

name: Geder
dictNote: A walled place, (Josh. 12:13), perhaps the same as Gederah or Gedor (15:58).

name: Raddai
dictNote: The fifth of Jesse's seven sons, and so a brother of David (1 Chronicles 2:14).

name: Kartah
dictNote: City, a town in the tribe of Zebulun assigned to the Levites of the family of Merari (Josh. 21:34). It is identical with Kattath (19:15), and perhaps also with Kitron (Judg. 1:30).

name: Ami
dictNote: Listed among the descendants of Solomon's servants who returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel; the parallel list in Nehemiah gives the name as Amon (Ezra 2:57; Nehemiah 7:59).

name: Senazar
dictNote: A son of Jeconiah, also called Jehoiachin, the exiled king of Judah, listed in the royal genealogy of David's line preserved after the Babylonian captivity (1 Chronicles 3:18).

name: Beth-diblathaim
note: Beth-Diblathajim, a place East of the Jordan
dictNote: House of two cakes of figs, a city of Moab, upon which Jeremiah (48:22) denounced destruction. It is called also Almon-diblathaim (Num. 33:46) and Diblath (Ezek. 6:14). (R.V., “Diblah.”)

name: Dibri
dictNote: A Danite, father of Shelomith, whose son by an Egyptian father was stoned for blasphemy in the wilderness, an episode that prompted the law on blasphemy recorded in Leviticus (Leviticus 24:10-11).

name: Sheminith
dictNote: Sheminith, meaning “eighth,” is a musical direction rather than a personal name, appearing in the titles of Psalms 6 and 12 and in the description of Levitical musicians in Chronicles. Its exact meaning is debated; most understand it as an instruction to play or sing in a lower octave or register (1 Chronicles 15:21).

name: Eranites
note: an Eranite or descendant (collectively) of Eran

name: Tohu
dictNote: An ancestor of Samuel in the genealogy of the prophet's Ephraimite Levite family, several generations before Samuel's father Elkanah (1 Samuel 1:1).

name: Haruphite
note: a Charuphite or inhabitant of Charuph (or Chariph)
dictNote: A native of Hariph; an epithet given to Shephatiah, one of those who joined David at Ziklag (1 Chr. 12:5).

name: Sharar
dictNote: Father of Ahiam, one of David's mighty warriors; the parallel list in Chronicles gives the name as Sacar (2 Samuel 23:33; 1 Chronicles 11:35).

name: Beth-car
dictNote: Sheep-house, a place to which the Israelites pursued the Philistines west from Mizpeh (1 Sam. 7:11).

name: Erites
note: an Erite (collectively) or descendants of Eri

name: Geshan
dictNote: A descendant of Caleb through his son Jahdai, listed in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chronicles 2:47).

name: Meri-baal
dictNote: An alternate Hebrew spelling of Merib-baal, the name Chronicles uses for Jonathan's son, known in the books of Samuel as Mephibosheth (1 Chronicles 9:40; compare 2 Samuel 4:4).

name: Shage
dictNote: Father of Jonathan the Hararite, one of David's mighty warriors (1 Chronicles 11:34).

name: Beth-rapha
dictNote: A name in the genealogy of Judah, listed as a son of Eshton in the line descended from Chelub (1 Chronicles 4:12).

name: Baale of Judah
dictNote: Lords of Judah, a city in the tribe of Judah from which David brought the ark into Jerusalem (2 Sam. 6:2). Elsewhere (1 Chr. 13:6) called Kirjath-jearim. (See BAALAH.)

name: Apollonia
note: from G622 (ἀπόλλυμι)); Apollonia, a place in Macedonia

dictNote: A city of Macedonia between Amphipolis and Thessalonica, from which it was distant about 36 miles. Paul and Silas passed through it on their way to Thessalonica (Acts 17:1).

name: Dimon
dictNote: (river bed), The waters of, some streams on the east of the Dead Sea, in the land of Moab, against which Isaiah uttered denunciation. (Isaiah 15:9) Gesenius conjectures that the two names Dimon and Dibon are the same.

name: Hushah
dictNote: A name appearing in the genealogies of Judah, associated with the descendants of Ezer (1 Chronicles 4:4).

name: Neiel
dictNote: Dwelling-place of God, a town in the territory of Asher, near its southern border (Josh. 19:27). It has been identified with the ruin Y’anin, near the outlet of the Wady esh Sha-ghur, less than 2 miles north of Kabul, and 16 miles east of Caesarea.

name: Homam
dictNote: An Edomite name in the genealogy of Esau's descendants through Seir the Horite; the parallel list in Genesis gives the form Hemam (1 Chronicles 1:39; Genesis 36:22).

name: Galatian
note: a Galatian or inhabitant of Galatia

name: Jubal

(10) From this Jubal, not improbably, came Jobel , the trumpet of Jobel or Jubilee : that large and loud musical instrument, used in proclaiming the liberty at the Year of Jubilee .

dictNote: Son of Lamech and Adah, in the line of Cain, remembered as the ancestor of all who play the lyre and pipe, making him the Bible's first named musician (Genesis 4:21).

name: Shihon
dictNote: Overturning, a town of Issachar (Josh. 19:19).

name: Jeberechiah
dictNote: Father of a Zechariah whom Isaiah took as a witness when the prophet inscribed a tablet during the reign of King Ahaz (Isaiah 8:2).

name: Machbanai
note: a Macbannite or native of Macbena
dictNote: One of the Gadite warriors, skilled with shield and spear, who defected to join David while he was still an outlaw hiding from Saul in the wilderness (1 Chronicles 12:8, 13).

name: Amphipolis
note: a city surrounded by a river; Amphipolis, a place in Macedonia
dictNote: City on both sides, a Macedonian city, a great Roman military station, through which Paul and Silas passed on their way from Philippi to Thessalonica, a distance of 33 Roman miles from Philippi (Acts 17:1).

name: Chelubai
dictNote: Son of Hezron and also called Caleb, this figure heads a branch of Judah's genealogy in Chronicles; he is a different man from the more famous Caleb son of Jephunneh, the spy who entered Canaan with Joshua (1 Chronicles 2:9, 18, 42).

name: Jedidah

secondTemple.excerpt: His mother was of the city of Boscath; and her name was Jedidah.

dictNote: Wife of King Amon of Judah and mother of Josiah, remembered as one of Judah's most thoroughgoing religious reformers (2 Kings 22:1).

name: Zeruah
dictNote: Mother of Jeroboam, who became the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel after the nation split following Solomon's death (1 Kings 11:26).

name: Shamhuth
dictNote: Commander of the fifth division of David's army, serving one month each year in the king's rotating military schedule (1 Chronicles 27:8).

name: Hashabnah
dictNote: One of the leaders who sealed the covenant of renewed obedience to the law that Nehemiah led the returned exiles to affirm (Nehemiah 10:25-26).

name: Elonites
note: an Elonite or descendant (collectively) of Elon

name: Mozah
dictNote: An issuing of water, a city of Benjamin (Josh. 18:26).

name: Shulamite
note: peaceful (with the article always prefixed, making it a pet name); the Shulammith, an epithet of Solomon's queen
dictNote: The same, as some think, with “Shunammite,” from “Shunem:” otherwise, the import of the word is uncertain (Cant. 6:13; R.V., “Shulammite”).

name: Madian
note: Madian (i.e. Midian), a region of Arabia

secondTemple.excerpt: Zambran, and Jazar, and Madan, and Madian, and Josabak, and Sous.

dictNote: (Acts 7:29) [Midian]

name: Ashpenaz

dictNote: Chief official over Nebuchadnezzar's court eunuchs, responsible for selecting and training young Judean nobles, including Daniel and his three companions, for royal service in Babylon (Daniel 1:3).

name: Parmenas
dictNote: One of the seven men chosen by the Jerusalem church to oversee the daily distribution of food to widows, freeing the apostles to focus on prayer and preaching (Acts 6:5).

name: Mishael

secondTemple.excerpt: 1 ff.); by Nadab and Abihu leaving their coats (or irrational parts) for Mishael and Elzaphan (Lev.

dictNote: Mishael was one of Daniel's three friends, renamed Meshach in Babylon, who survived Nebuchadnezzar's fiery furnace after refusing to worship his golden image.

name: Othni
dictNote: Son of Shemaiah, a temple gatekeeper of notable ability during David's reign (1 Chronicles 26:6-7).

name: Apharsite
note: an Apherasite or inhabitant of an unknown region of Assyria

name: Haziel
dictNote: A Levite of the Gershonite clan, descended through Shimei, listed among those organized for temple service under David (1 Chronicles 23:9).

name: Sippai
dictNote: A Philistine warrior of great size, one of the descendants of the Rephaim, killed by David's soldier Sibbechai at Gezer; the parallel account in Samuel calls him Saph (1 Chronicles 20:4; 2 Samuel 21:18).

name: Sharuhen
dictNote: (refuge of grace), a town named in (Joshua 19:6) only among those which were in Jadah to Simeon. It is identified with Sheriah a large ruin in the south country, northwest of Beersheba.

name: Zuzims
note: Zuzites, an aboriginal tribe of Palestine
dictNote: The Zuzim were a people living east of the Jordan whom the invading coalition led by Chedorlaomer defeated in the campaign that eventually swept up Lot at Sodom (Genesis 14:5). Some identify them with the Zamzummim, a similarly obscure people the Ammonites are said to have displaced from the same region (Deuteronomy 2:20).

name: Mecherathite
note: a Mekerathite, or inhabitant of Mekerah

name: Adamah
dictNote: Red earth, a fortified city of Naphtali, probably the modern Damieh, on the west side of the sea of Tiberias (Josh. 19:33, 36).

name: Bene-barak
note: sons of lightning, Bene-berak, a place in Palestine

name: Hazar-hatticon
dictNote: Village of the midway, a place near Hamath in the confines of Hauran (Ezek. 47:16), probably on the north brow of Hermon.

name: Beeshterah
note: Beeshterah, a place East of the Jordan
dictNote: (house of Ashterah), one of the two cities allotted to the sons of Gershon out of the tribe of Manasseh beyond Jordan. (Joshua 21:27) Probably identical with Ashtaroth. (1 Chronicles 6:71)

name: Zair
dictNote: Little, a place probably east of the Dead Sea, where Joram discomfited the host of Edom who had revolted from him (2 Kings 8:21).

name: Beth-gamul
note: Beth-Gamul, a place East of the Jordan
dictNote: Camel-house, a city in the “plain country” of Moab denounced by the prophet (Jer. 48:23); probably the modern Um-el-Jemal, near Bozrah, one of the deserted cities of the Hauran.

name: Shuham
dictNote: Son of Dan and ancestor of the Shuhamite clan, one of the tribal divisions counted in the wilderness census (Numbers 26:42-43).

name: Heleph
dictNote: Exchange, a city on the north border of Naphtali (Josh. 19:33).

name: Hodevah
dictNote: Hodevah is an alternate spelling of Hodaviah, head of a family of Levites who returned from Babylonian exile with Zerubbabel (Neh. 7:43). Nothing further is recorded of him.

name: Shua

secondTemple.excerpt: And she bare him six sons, Zimram, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah, in the two weeks of years.

dictNote: Shua was a daughter of Heber, of the tribe of Asher, listed among his children in the tribal genealogy of 1 Chronicles 7:32. She is a different person from the Canaanite woman named Shua whose daughter married Judah in Genesis 38.

name: Naam
dictNote: Naam was one of the sons of Caleb son of Jephunneh, named in the genealogy of Judah (1 Chr. 4:15). He appears only in this single genealogical notice.

name: Keziz
dictNote: Abrupt; cut off, a city of the tribe of Benjamin (Josh. 18:21).

name: Bozez
dictNote: Bozez was not a person but one of two rocky crags, the other named Seneh, that flanked the narrow pass through which Jonathan and his armor-bearer climbed to surprise the Philistine garrison at Michmash (1 Sam. 14:4-5). The steep terrain around Michmash still matches the description in the text.

name: Sheal
dictNote: Sheal was one of the sons of Bani listed among the Israelites who had married foreign wives during the exile and agreed to separate from them under Ezra's reform (Ezra 10:29). Nothing more is recorded of him.

name: Bozrah
dictNote: In Micah's oracle of restoration, the remnant of Israel is pictured gathered together like sheep, and the text reads literally "as the sheep of Bozrah" (Micah 2:12). Interpreters differ over whether this points to the famous Edomite city of Bozrah and its pastures, described in the separate place record for Bozrah, or whether the Hebrew word functions here as a common noun for a sheepfold rather than a proper name.

name: Jorim
dictNote: Jorim was the son of Matthat, listed among the ancestors of Jesus in Luke's genealogy (Luke 3:29), which traces David's line through his son Nathan rather than through Solomon as Matthew's genealogy does. Nothing else is recorded of him.

name: Ismachiah
dictNote: Ismachiah was a Levite appointed as one of the overseers of the freewill offerings, tithes, and dedicated gifts brought into the temple during King Hezekiah's religious reforms, serving alongside Cononiah and Shimei under the high priest Azariah (2 Chr. 31:12-13).

name: Ahian

dictNote: A community; alliance. (1.) A city in the south end of the valley of Eshcol, about midway between Jerusalem and Beersheba, from which it is distant about 20 miles in a straight line. It was built “seven years before Zoan in Egypt” (Gen. 13:18; Num. 13:22). It still exists under the same name, and is one of the most ancient cities in the world. Its earlier name was Kirjath-arba (Gen. 23:2; Josh. 14:15; 15:3). But “Hebron would appear to have been the original name of the city, and it was not till after Abraham’s stay there that it received the name Kirjath-arba, who [i.e., Arba] was not the founder but the conqueror of the city, having led thither the tribe of the Anakim, to which he belonged. It retained this name till it came into the possession of Caleb, when the Israelites restored the original name Hebron” (Keil, Com.). The name of this city does not occur in any of the prophets or in the New Testament. It is found about forty times in the Old. It was the favorite home of Abraham. Here he pitched his tent under the oaks of Mamre, by which name it came afterwards to be known; and here Sarah died, and was buried in the cave of Machpelah (Gen. 23:17-20), which he bought from Ephron the Hittite. From this place the patriarch departed for Egypt by way of Beersheba (37:14; 46:1). It was taken by Joshua and given to Caleb (Josh. 10:36, 37; 12:10; 14:13). It became a Levitical city and a city of refuge (20:7; 21:11). When David became king of Judah this was his royal residence, and he resided here for seven and a half years (2 Sam. 5:5); and here he was anointed as king over all Israel (2 Sam. 2:1-4, 11; 1 Kings 2:11). It became the residence also of the rebellious Absalom (2 Sam. 15:10), who probably expected to find his chief support in the tribe of Judah, now called el-Khulil. In one part of the modern city is a great mosque, which is built over the grave of Machpelah. The first European who was permitted to enter this mosque was the Prince of Wales in 1862. It was also visited by the Marquis of Bute in 1866, and by the late Emperor Frederick of Germany (then Crown-Prince of Prussia) in 1869. One of the largest oaks in Palestine is found in the valley of Eshcol, about 3 miles north of the town. It is supposed by some to be the tree under which Abraham pitched his tent, and is called “Abraham’s oak.” (See OAK.) (2.) The third son of Kohath the Levite (Ex. 6:18; 1 Chr. 6:2, 18). (3.) 1 Chr. 2:42, 43. (4.) A town in the north border of Asher (Josh. 19:28).

name: Ahiram

name: Hashubah

name: Shelesh

name: Maarath
dictNote: Desolation, a place in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:59), probably the modern village Beit Ummar, 6 miles north of Hebron.

name: Elmodam
dictNote: Elmodam was the son of Er, listed among the ancestors of Jesus in Luke's genealogy, in the line descended from David's son Nathan (Luke 3:28).

name: Abi
dictNote: Abi was the mother of King Hezekiah of Judah and wife of King Ahaz, identified as the daughter of a Zechariah (2 Kings 18:2). The parallel record in 2 Chronicles 29:1 calls her Abijah.

name: Hadassah
dictNote: Hadassah was the Hebrew name of Esther before she took the Persian name by which she became known as queen to King Ahasuerus. Orphaned young, she was raised by her cousin Mordecai in Susa (Esther 2:7).

name: Hanes
dictNote: A place in Egypt mentioned only in Isa. 30:4 in connection with a reproof given to the Jews for trusting in Egypt. It was considered the same as Tahpanhes, a fortified town on the eastern frontier, but has been also identified as Ahnas-el-Medeeneh, 70 miles from Cairo.

name: Lahmi

dictNote: Brother of the Philistine giant Goliath, killed by Elhanan son of Jair during a battle between David's men and the Philistines (1 Chronicles 20:5).

name: Igdaliah
dictNote: Igdaliah was called "the man of God," an otherwise unknown prophet or holy figure whose son Hanan had a chamber in the temple where Jeremiah gathered the Rechabites to test their obedience to their ancestral vow (Jer. 35:1-4).

name: Zoheleth

dictNote: Zoheleth, meaning "the serpent stone," was a rock near the spring of En-rogel outside Jerusalem where Adonijah, David's son, held a sacrificial feast to have himself proclaimed king while David lay dying, deliberately leaving out Solomon, Nathan, and Solomon's other supporters (1 Kings 1:9-10). name: Jashen
dictNote: Jashen was the father of several warriors in David's elite fighting force, listed among his mighty men (2 Sam. 23:32); he is called Hashem in the parallel list at 1 Chronicles 11:34.

name: Lasea
dictNote: (Acts 27:8) a city of Crete, the ruins of which were discovered in 1856, a few miles to the eastward of Fair Havens.

name: Ishod
dictNote: Ishod was a son of Hammoleketh, of the half-tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan, named in the tribal genealogy of Manasseh (1 Chr. 7:18).

name: Aharhel
dictNote: Aharhel is named as a descendant of Harum's clan in a terse and difficult fragment of Judah's genealogy (1 Chr. 4:8). Little else can be reconstructed about his family from the text.

name: Aharah
dictNote: Aharah was the third son of Benjamin, listed in the tribal genealogy of Benjamin (1 Chr. 8:1). He is likely the same figure called Ahiram in Numbers 26:38 and Aher in 1 Chronicles 7:12, since the lists of Benjamin's sons vary somewhat between Genesis, Numbers, and Chronicles.

name: Dodai
dictNote: Dodai was an Ahohite who commanded the army division serving King David during the second month of the year, one of twelve divisions that rotated monthly military duty (1 Chr. 27:4). He may be the father of Eleazar, one of David's three chief warriors (2 Sam. 23:9).

name: Bether
dictNote: Dissection or separation, certain mountains mentioned in Cant. 2:17; probably near Lebanon.

name: Maleleel
dictNote: Maleleel is the Greek form of Mahalalel, a descendant of Seth before the flood, listed among the ancestors of Jesus in Luke's genealogy, which traces the line back through Noah to Adam (Luke 3:37; cf. Gen. 5:12-17).

name: Beer-elim
note: Beer-Elim, a place in the Desert
dictNote: Well of heroes, probably the name given to Beer, the place where the chiefs of Israel dug a well (Num. 21:16; Isa. 15:8).

name: Adronicus
note: man of victory; Andronicos, an Israelite
dictNote: This entry's name reflects a likely data spelling of Andronicus, a Jewish Christian and relative or fellow countryman of Paul whom Paul greets in Romans 16:7 along with Junia, calling the pair "outstanding among the apostles" and noting that they had been believers in Christ before Paul's own conversion.

name: Elead
dictNote: Elead was an Ephraimite killed by the men of Gath while raiding their livestock, one of several sons of Ephraim who died in the raid and whose loss caused their father Ephraim to mourn for many days (1 Chr. 7:20-22).

name: Jakeh
dictNote: Jakeh appears only as the father of Agur, whose sayings make up Proverbs 30. Nothing else about him is recorded in scripture, and Agur's own identity and homeland (possibly Massa, an Arabian tribe) remain debated among scholars.

name: Maasiai
dictNote: Maasiai was a priest listed among those who resettled Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, as recorded in the genealogical roll of 1 Chronicles 9. Nothing further is known of him beyond his place in that list.

name: Phygellus
dictNote: Phygellus was a Christian in the Roman province of Asia named by Paul as one who turned away from him during his final imprisonment in Rome, alongside a man named Hermogenes (2 Tim. 1:15). name: Middin

name: Telah

name: Ahban
dictNote: Ahban was a son of Abishur and his wife Abihail, listed in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles 2. Nothing further is known of him.

name: Ziz

name: Hashem
dictNote: Hashem was a Gizonite whose sons are named among David's mighty men in 1 Chronicles 11:34. The parallel list in 2 Samuel 23:32 gives the name differently, as Jashen, reflecting the textual variants common between these two overlapping rosters.

name: Mearah
dictNote: A cave, a place in the northern boundary of Palestine (Josh. 13:4). This may be the cave of Jezzin in Lebanon, 10 miles east of Sidon, on the Damascus road; or probably, as others think, Mogheirizeh, north-east of Sidon.

name: Barjesus
note: son of Jesus (or Joshua); Bar-jesus, an Israelite
dictNote: Bar-Jesus was a Jewish false prophet and magician attached to the court of Sergius Paulus, the Roman proconsul of Cyprus (Acts 13:6). His name means son of Jesus, an ironic title for a man Paul denounced as a son of the devil.

name: Misham
dictNote: Misham was a Benjamite, one of the sons of Elpaal, listed in the tribal genealogy of 1 Chronicles 8. Nothing further is recorded about him.

name: Uzzen-sherah
dictNote: A town probably near Beth-horon. It derived its name from the daughter of Ephraim (1 Chr. 7:24).

name: Sharai
dictNote: Sharai was one of the men listed in Ezra 10 who had married foreign wives during the postexilic period and agreed to separate from them as part of Ezra's covenant reform. He is identified as one of the sons of Bani.

name: Piltai
dictNote: Piltai was head of the priestly family of Moadiah in the days of the high priest Joiakim, in the generation after the return from Babylonian exile, as recorded in the priestly and Levitical family lists of Nehemiah 12. Nothing further is known of him.

name: Ezbai
dictNote: Ezbai was the father of Naarai, one of David's mighty men listed in 1 Chronicles 11:37. Nothing further is recorded about him.

dictNote: Babylonia was the ancient region and empire of lower Mesopotamia, centered on the Euphrates and Tigris valleys with Babylon as its capital. Its armies conquered the kingdom of Judah in 586 BC, destroyed Jerusalem and Solomon's temple, and deported much of the population, an event corroborated by Babylonian ration tablets that name the exiled Judean king Jehoiachin among captives at Nebuchadnezzar's court. Babylonia's own dominance ended when it fell to Cyrus the Persian in 539 BC, an event the Cyrus Cylinder itself commemorates. In Ezra 4:9 the name refers to Babylonian officials and settlers who opposed the rebuilding of Jerusalem after the exile.

name: Meonothai
dictNote: Meonothai was a son of Othniel, the judge and younger brother of Caleb, and is listed in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles 4:14 as the father of Ophrah. Nothing further is recorded about him.

name: Anammelech
dictNote: Anammelech was a deity worshipped by the people of Sepharvaim, a Mesopotamian population the Assyrians resettled in Samaria after deporting the northern kingdom of Israel in 722 BC (2 Kings 17:31). The colonists reportedly burned their children in fire to Anammelech and its companion god Adrammelech, a practice associated in the ancient Near East with Molech worship. Assyrian resettlement policy of this kind is well attested in Assyrian royal inscriptions, including those of Sargon II, who claims credit for Samaria's conquest.

name: Siphmoth
dictNote: Fruitful places, some unknown place in the south, where David found friends when he fled from Saul (1 Sam. 30:28).

Later Christian writers linked his name to the Nicolaitans condemned in Revelation 2, though the New Testament itself does not connect him to that group.

name: Tryphosa
dictNote: Tryphosa was a Christian woman in Rome whom Paul greets alongside Tryphena in Romans 16:12, commending both as women who work hard in the Lord. Their similar names suggest they may have been sisters, since such paired names occur among household members and freedwomen in Roman inscriptions of the period. Nothing further is known of her.

name: Bartimaeus
note: son of Timæus (or the unclean); Bar-timæus, an Israelite
dictNote: Bartimaeus was a blind beggar at Jericho, son of a man named Timaeus, whose sight Jesus restored after Bartimaeus called out to him as Son of David (Mark 10:46-52). His persistence despite the crowd's attempts to silence him is presented as an example of faith. The parallel account in Matthew 20:30 mentions two unnamed blind men, while Luke 18:35 places the healing as Jesus approached rather than left the city.

name: Ibri
dictNote: Ibri was a Merarite Levite of the family of Jaaziah, listed among the Levitical divisions organized in the time of David (1 Chronicles 24:27). Nothing further is recorded about him.

name: Madmenah
dictNote: Ibid., a town in Benjamin, not far from Jerusalem, towards the north (Isa. 10:31). The same Hebrew word occurs in Isa. 25:10, where it is rendered “dunghill.” This verse has, however, been interpreted as meaning “that Moab will be trodden down by Jehovah as teben [broken straw] is trodden to fragments on the threshing-floors of Madmenah.”

name: Aridatha
dictNote: Aridatha was one of the ten sons of Haman, the Persian official who plotted to destroy the Jews of the empire under King Ahasuerus. He was killed along with his brothers when the Jews defended themselves on the day Haman had set for their destruction, and his body was later hanged (Esther 9:8-10).

name: Ahimoth
dictNote: Ahimoth was a Kohathite Levite named in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles 6. The same genealogy later gives the name as Mahath, reflecting the sort of variant spellings common in these priestly family records.

dictNote: Jehoiachin was a king of Judah who reigned only three months before surrendering to Nebuchadnezzar's siege and being taken captive to Babylon along with much of Jerusalem's elite. He remained a prisoner for thirty-seven years until a new Babylonian king released him and gave him a regular place at the royal table for the rest of his life, a small note of hope that closes out 2 Kings.

name: Dan-jaan
dictNote: Woodland Dan, a place probably somewhere in the direction of Dan, near the sources of the Jordan (2 Sam. 24:6). The LXX. and the Vulgate read “Dan-ja’ar”, i.e., “Dan in the forest.”

name: Jehosheba

secondTemple.excerpt: Ahaziah had a sister, by the same father, whose name was Jehosheba ; and she was married to the High Priest Jehoiada.

dictNote: Jehosheba was a daughter of King Jehoram of Judah and, according to 2 Chronicles 22:11, wife of the high priest Jehoiada. When the usurper Athaliah moved to kill the entire royal family after her son Ahaziah's death, Jehosheba hid the infant prince Joash in the temple for six years, preserving the Davidic line (2 Kings 11:2-3). She is called Jehoshabeath in 2 Chronicles 22:11.

name: Nagge
dictNote: Nagge appears in Luke's genealogy of Jesus as an ancestor in the line through Mary, listed as the father of Esli and son of Maath (Luke 3:25). Nothing else is known of him.

name: Jehucal
dictNote: Jehucal, also called Jucal, was an official King Zedekiah sent, along with the priest Zephaniah, to ask the prophet Jeremiah to pray for the besieged kingdom during the final Babylonian siege of Jerusalem (Jer. 37:3). He later appears among the officials who had Jeremiah thrown into a cistern for prophesying the city's fall (Jer. 38:1-6).

name: Maktesh
note: dell; the Maktesh, a place in Jerusalem
dictNote: Mortar, a place in or near Jerusalem inhabited by silver merchants (Zeph. 1:11). It has been conjectured that it was the “Phoenician quarter” of the city, where the traders of that nation resided, after the Oriental custom.

name: Timon
dictNote: Timon was one of the seven men chosen by the Jerusalem church to administer the daily distribution to widows in Acts 6:5. Nothing further is known of him.

name: Rama
note: Rama (i.e. Ramah), a place in Palestine
dictNote: (Matt. 2:18), the Greek form of Ramah. (1.) A city first mentioned in Josh. 18:25, near Gibeah of Benjamin. It was fortified by Baasha, king of Israel (1 Kings 15:17-22; 2 Chr. 16:1-6). Asa, king of Judah, employed Benhadad the Syrian king to drive Baasha from this city (1 Kings 15:18, 20). Isaiah (10:29) refers to it, and also Jeremiah, who was once a prisoner there among the other captives of Jerusalem when it was taken by Nebuchadnezzar (Jer. 39:8-12; 40:1). Rachel, whose tomb lies close to Bethlehem, is represented as weeping in Ramah (Jer. 31:15) for her slaughtered children. This prophecy is illustrated and fulfilled in the re-awakening of Rachel’s grief at the slaughter of the infants in Bethlehem (Matt. 2:18). It is identified with the modern village of er-Ram, between Gibeon and Beeroth, about 5 miles due north of Jerusalem. (See SAMUEL.) (2.) A town identified with Rameh, on the border of Asher, about 13 miles south-east of Tyre, “on a solitary hill in the midst of a basin of green fields” (Josh. 19:29). (3.) One of the “fenced cities” of Naphtali (Josh. 19:36), on a mountain slope, about seven and a half miles west-south-west of Safed, and 15 miles west of the north end of the Sea of Galilee, the present large and well-built village of Rameh. (4.) The same as Ramathaim-zophim (q.v.), a town of Mount Ephraim (1 Sam. 1:1, 19). (5.) The same as Ramoth-gilead (q.v.), 2 Kings 8:29; 2 Chr. 22:6.

name: Tochen
dictNote: Measured, a town of Simeon (1 Chr. 4:32).

name: Abed-nego
note: Abed-Nego, the Babylonian name of one of Daniel's companions
dictNote: Abednego was the Babylonian name given to Azariah, one of Daniel's three friends who were thrown into a fiery furnace in Babylon for refusing to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image and emerged completely unharmed.

name: Jeshishai
dictNote: Jeshishai appears in the genealogy of the Gadite settlers of Gilead in 1 Chronicles 5:14. Nothing further is recorded about him.

name: Hupham
dictNote: Hupham was a son of Benjamin and founder of the Huphamite clan, counted in the wilderness census of Numbers 26:39. He is also called Huppim in Genesis 46:21 and 1 Chronicles 7:12.

name: Chislon
dictNote: Chislon was the father of Elidad, the leader from the tribe of Benjamin chosen to help apportion the land of Canaan among the tribes after the conquest (Numbers 34:21). Nothing further is known of him.

name: Clauda
dictNote: Clauda, also spelled Cauda, was a small island off the southwest coast of Crete that Paul's ship passed under the shelter of during the storm that eventually wrecked it on Malta (Acts 27:16). Sailors used its lee to haul in the ship's boat and undergird the vessel with ropes before running before the wind. The island is identified with modern Gavdos, the southernmost point of Europe.

name: Hazelelponi
dictNote: Hazelelponi was a woman named in the genealogy of Judah as the sister of the sons of Etam (1 Chronicles 4:3). Nothing further is recorded about her.

name: Avim
note: Avvim (as inhabited by Avvites), a place in Palestine (with the article prefix)
dictNote: A people dwelling in Hazerim, or “the villages” or “encampments” on the south-west corner of the sea-coast (Deut. 2:23). They were subdued and driven northward by the Caphtorim. A trace of them is afterwards found in Josh. 13:3, where they are called Avites.
