dictNote: A Christian at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:10), and styles “approved in Christ.”

name: Suchathite
note: a Sukathite or descendant of an unknown Israelite named Sukah

name: Punites
note: a Punite (collectively) or descendants of an unknown Pun

name: Beninu
dictNote: (our son), a Levite; one of those who sealed the covenant with Nehemiah. (Nehemiah 10:13,14)

name: Rhegium

secondTemple.excerpt: And for any great or royal work that he ever did, which might be for the present and for future ages, nobody can name any such, but only the haven that he made about Rhegium and Sicily, for the reception of the ships that brought corn from Egypt; which was indeed a work without dispute very great in itself, and of very great advantage to the navigation.

dictNote: Breach, a town in the south of Italy, on the Strait of Messina, at which Paul touched on his way to Rome (Acts 28:13). It is now called Rheggio.

name: Jalon
dictNote: Lodger, the last of the four sons of Ezra, of the tribe of Judah (1 Chr. 4:17).

name: Manaen
dictNote: Consoler, a Christian teacher at Antioch. Nothing else is known of him beyond what is stated in Acts 13:1, where he is spoken of as having been brought up with (Gr. syntrophos; rendered in R.V. “foster brother” of) Herod, i.e., Herod Antipas, the tetrach, who, with his brother Archelaus, was educated at Rome.

name: Gazez
note: Gazez, the name of two Israelites
dictNote: (shearer), a name which occurs twice in (1 Chronicles 2:46)—first as son of Caleb by Ephah his concubine, and second as son of Haran, the son of the same woman. The second is possibly only a repetition of the first (B.C. after 1688.)

name: Halhul
dictNote: Full of hollows, a town in the highlands of Judah (Josh. 15:58). It is now a small village of the same name, and is situated about 5 miles north-east of Hebron on the way to Jerusalem. There is an old Jewish tradition that Gad, David’s seer (2 Sam. 24:11), was buried here.

name: Aenon
dictNote: Springs, a place near Salim where John baptized (John 3:23). It was probably near the upper source of the Wady Far’ah, an open valley extending from Mount Ebal to the Jordan. It is full of springs. A place has been found called ‘Ainun, four miles north of the springs.

name: Syntyche
note: an accident; Syntyche, a Christian female
dictNote: Fortunate; affable, a female member of the church at Philippi, whom Paul beseeches to be of one mind with Euodias (Phil. 4:2, 3).

name: Uel
dictNote: (will of God), one of the family of Bani, who during the captivity had married a foreign wife. (Ezra 10:34) (B.C. 458.)

name: Beth-emek
dictNote: (house of the valley), a place on or near the border of Asher, on the north side of which was the ravine of Jiphthah-el (Joshua 19:27)

name: Aphekah
dictNote: (strong place), a city of Judah, in the mountains (Joshua 15:53) probably the same as Aphek, 1.

name: Jearim
dictNote: Forests, a mountain on the border of Judah (Josh. 15:10).

name: Succothbenoth
note: booths of (the) daughters; brothels, i.e. idoalatrous tents for impure purpose
dictNote: Occurs only in (2 Kings 17:30) It has generally been supposed that this term is pure Hebrew, and signifies the tents of daughters; which some explain as “the booths in which the daughters of the Babylonians prostituted themselves in honor of their idol,” others as “small tabernacles in which were contained images of female deities.” Sir H. Rawlinson thinks that Succoth-benoth represents the Chaldaean goddess Zerbanit, the wife of Merodach, who was especially worshipped at Babylon.

name: Sebat
dictNote: The eleventh month of the Hebrew year, extending from the new moon of February to that of March (Zech. 1:7). Assyrian sabatu, “storm.” (See MONTH.)

name: Mitylene
note: Mitylene (or Mytilene), a town on the island of Lesbos

secondTemple.excerpt: Now Agrippa was [about this time] sent to succeed Caesar in the government of the countries beyond the Ionian Sea, upon whom Herod lighted when he was wintering about Mitylene, for he had been his particular friend and companion, and then returned into Judea again.

dictNote: The chief city of the island of Lesbos, on its east coast, in the AEgean Sea. Paul, during his third missionary journey, touched at this place on his way from Corinth to Judea (Acts 20:14), and here tarried for a night. It lies between Assos and Chios. It is now under the Turkish rule, and bears the name of Metelin.

name: Ben-oni
note: Ben-Oni, the original name of Benjamin
dictNote: (son of my sorrow). (Genesis 35:18) [Benjamin, Benjamin, The Tribe Of]

name: Bakbakkar
dictNote: (admirable), a Levite, apparently a descendant of Asaph. (1 Chronicles 9:15) (B.C.588.)

name: Arisai
dictNote: (lion-like), eighth son of Haman. (Esther 9:9)

name: Jagur
dictNote: Place of sojourn, a city on the southern border of Judah (Josh. 15:21).

name: Hodesh
dictNote: (new moon), a woman named in the genealogies of Benjamin, (1 Chronicles 8:9) as the wife of Shaharaim.

name: Magpiash
dictNote: (moth-killer) one of the heads of the people who signed the covenant with Nehemiah. (Nehemiah 10:20) The same as Magbish in (Ezra 2:30)

name: Hemdan
dictNote: (pleasant), the eldest son of Dishon, son of Anah the Horite. (Genesis 36:26) [Amram, 2] (B.C. about 1500.)

name: Beth-gader
dictNote: (house of the wall), doubtless a place, though it occurs in the genealogies of Judah as if a person. (1 Chronicles 2:51)

name: Emmanuel
note: God with us; Emmanuel, a name of Christ
dictNote: God with us, Matt. 1:23). (See IMMANUEL.)

name: Arieh
dictNote: The lion, the name of one of the body-guard slain with Pekahiah at Samaria (2 Kings 15:25) by the conspirator Pekah.

name: Jashubites
note: a Jashubite, or descendant of Jashub

name: Hiddai
dictNote: Rejoicing of Jehovah, one of David’s thirty-seven guards (2 Sam. 23:30).

name: Bidkar

secondTemple.excerpt: Jehu also gave orders to Bidkar, the captain of the third part of his army, to cast the dead body of Joram into the field of Naboth: putting him in mind of the Prophecy which Elijah prophesyed to Ahab his father, when he had slain Naboth; that both he

dictNote: (son of stabbing, i.e, one who stabs), Jehu’s “captain,” originally his fellow officer, (2 Kings 9:25) who completed the sentence on Jehoram, son of Ahab.

name: Lebonah
dictNote: Frankincense, a town near Shiloh, on the north side of Bethel (Judg. 21:19). It has been identified with el-Lubban, to the south of Nablus.

name: Riphath
note: Riphath, a grandson of Japheth and his descendants

secondTemple.excerpt: So did Riphath found the Ripheans, now called Paphlagonians; and Thrugramma, the Thrugrammeans, who, as the Greeks resolved, were named Phrygians.

dictNote: A crusher, Gomer’s second son (Gen. 10:3), supposed to have been the ancestor of the Paphlagonians.

name: Shiphrah

secondTemple.excerpt: (128) Moses appears to me to have intended figuratively to represent these virtues when he calls the midwives of the Egyptians, Shiphrah and Puah, {45}{#ex 1:15.} for the name Shiphrah, being interpreted, means \"a little bird,\" and Puah means \"red.\" Now it is the especial property of divine wisdom, like a bird, to be always soaring on high; but it is

dictNote: Beauty, one of the Egyptian midwives (Ex. 1:15).

name: Accho
note: Akko (from its situation on a bay)
dictNote: Sultry or sandy, a town and harbour of Phoenicia, in the tribe of Asher, but never acquired by them (Judg. 1:31). It was known to the ancient Greeks and Romans by the name of Ptolemais, from Ptolemy the king of Egypt, who rebuilt it about B.C. 100. Here Paul landed on his last journey to Jerusalem (Acts 21:7). During the crusades of the Middle Ages it was called Acra; and subsequently, on account of its being occupied by the Knights Hospitallers of Jerusalem, it was called St. Jean d’Acre, or simply Acre.

name: On
dictNote: Light; the sun, (Gen. 41:45, 50), the great seat of sun-worship, called also Bethshemesh (Jer. 43:13) and Aven (Ezek. 30:17), stood on the east bank of the Nile, a few miles north of Memphis, and near Cairo, in the north-east. The Vulgate and the LXX. Versions have “Heliopolis” (“city of the sun”) instead of On in Genesis and of Aven in Ezekiel. The “city of destruction” Isaiah speaks of (19:18, marg. “of Heres;” Heb. ‘Ir-ha-heres, which some MSS. read Ir-ha-heres, i.e., “city of the sun”) may be the name given to On, the prophecy being that the time will come when that city which was known as the “city of the sun-god” shall become the “city of destruction” of the sun-god, i.e., when idolatry shall cease, and the worship of the true God be established. In ancient times this city was full of obelisks dedicated to the sun. Of these only one now remains standing. “Cleopatra’s Needle” was one of those which stood in this city in front of the Temple of Tum, i.e., “the sun.” It is now erected on the Thames Embankment, London. “It was at On that Joseph wooed and won the dark-skinned Asenath, the daughter of the high priest of its great temple.” This was a noted university town, and here Moses gained his acquaintance with “all the wisdom of the Egyptians.”

name: Libnites
note: a Libnite or descendants of Libni (collectively)

name: Josibiah
dictNote: (to whom God gives a dwelling), the father of Jehu, a Simeonite. (1 Chronicles 4:35)

name: Gezrites
note: a Grizite (collectively) or member of a native tribe in Palestine

name: Abelshittim
note: Abel hash-Shittim, a place in Palestine
dictNote: (the meadow of the acacias), in the “plains” of Moab, on the low level of the Jordan valley, opposite Jericho. The last resting-place of Israel before crossing the Jordan. (Numbers 33:49) The place is most frequently mentioned by its shorter name of Shittim. See Shittah Tree, Shittim, Shittim.

name: Jorah
dictNote: (the early rain), the ancestor of a family of 112 who returned from Babylon with Ezra. (Ezra 2:18) In (Nehemiah 7:24) he appears under the name Hariph, or more correctly the same family are represented as the Bene-Hariph.

name: Dizahab
note: Dizahab, a place in the Desert
dictNote: Region of gold, a place in the desert of Sinai, on the western shore of the Elanitic gulf (Deut. 1:1). It is now called Dehab.

name: Allon
note: Allon, an Israelite, also a place in Palestine
dictNote: Oak. (1.) The expression in the Authorized Version of Josh. 19:33, “from Allon to Zaanannim,” is more correctly rendered in the Revised Version, “from the oak in Zaanannim.” The word denotes some remarkable tree which stood near Zaanannim, and which served as a landmark. (2.) The son of Jedaiah, of the family of the Simeonites, who expelled the Hamites from the valley of Gedor (1 Chr. 4:37).

name: Shimeathites
note: a Shimathite (collectively) or descendants of Shimah

name: Philemon
dictNote: Philemon was a wealthy Christian, likely in Colossae, whose runaway slave Onesimus encountered Paul and became a believer, and Paul's short letter to Philemon appeals for Onesimus to be welcomed back without punishment, hinting that Paul would consider it a personal favor and even offering to cover any debt Onesimus owed.

name: Kushaiah
dictNote: (bow of Jehovah), the same as Kish or Kishi, the father of Ethan the Merarite. (1 Chronicles 15:17)

name: Sheth
dictNote: Tumult. (1.) “The children of Sheth” (Num. 24:17); R.V., “the sons of tumult,” which is probably the correct rendering, as there is no evidence that this is a proper name here. (2.) The antediluvian patriarch (1 Chr. 1:1).

name: Zaza
dictNote: Plenty, a descendant of Judah (1 Chr. 2:33).

name: Tryphena
dictNote: and Trypho’sa (luxurious), two Christian women at Rome, enumerated in the conclusion of St. Paul’s letter. (Romans 16:12) (A.D. 55.) They may have been sisters, but it is more likely that they were fellow deaconesses. We know nothing more of these two sister workers of the apostolic time.

name: Taanath-shiloh
dictNote: Approach to Shiloh, a place on the border of Ephraim (Josh. 16:6), probably the modern T’ana, a ruin 7 miles south-east of Shechem, on the ridge east of the Mukhnah plain.

name: Hamulites
note: a Chamulite (collectively) or descendants of Chamul

name: Samgar-nebo
dictNote: Be gracious, O Nebo! or a cup-bearer of Nebo, probably the title of Nergal-sharezer, one of the princes of Babylon (Jer. 39:3).

name: Gur-baal
dictNote: Sojourn of Baal, a place in Arabia (2 Chr. 26:7) where there was probably a temple of Baal.

name: Ittahkazin
dictNote: (time of the judge), one of the landmarks of the boundary of Zebulun. (Joshua 19:13) It has not been identified.

name: Semei

secondTemple.excerpt:
Testament of Levi, Chapter 12

12 1, 2 And Gersam took a wife, and she bare to him Lomni and Semei.

dictNote: Mentioned in the genealogy of our Lord (Luke 3:26).

name: Ozni
note: Ozni, an Israelite; also an Oznite (collectively), his descendant
dictNote: Hearing, one of the sons of Gad; also called Ezbon (Gen. 46:16; Num. 26:16).

name: Seneh
dictNote: The acacia; rock-thorn, the southern cliff in the Wady es-Suweinit, a valley south of Michmash, which Jonathan climbed with his armour-bearer (1 Sam. 14:4, 5). The rock opposite, on the other side of the wady, was called Bozez.

name: Shema
dictNote: Rumour. (1.) A Reubenite (1 Chr. 5:8). (2.) A Benjamite (1 Chr. 8:13). (3.) One who stood by Ezra when he read the law (Neh. 8:4). (4.) A town in the south of Judah (Josh. 15:26); the same as Sheba (ver. 5).

name: Zaphon
dictNote: (north), a place mentioned in the enumeration of the allotment of the tribe of Gad. (Joshua 13:27)

name: Hezeki
dictNote: (strong), a Benjamite, one of the Bene-Elpaal, a descendant of Shaaraim. (1 Chronicles 8:17) (B.C. 598.)

name: Meshullemeth
dictNote: Friend, the wife of Manasseh, and the mother of Amon (2 Kings 21:19), Kings of Judah.

name: Kallai
dictNote: (swift servant of Jehovah), a priest in the days of Joiakim the son of Jeshua. He represented the family of Sallai. (Nehemiah 12:20) (B.C. after 536.)

name: Cis
dictNote: the father of Saul, (Acts 13:21) usually called Kish.

name: Zereth
dictNote: (splendor), son of Ashur, the founder of Tekoa, by his wife Helah. (1 Chronicles 4:7) (B.C. 1440.)

name: Tebeth

6 [ Tebeth :] Casleu.

dictNote: (Esther 2:16), a word probably of Persian origin, denoting the cold time of the year; used by the later Jews as denoting the tenth month of the year. Assyrian tebituv, “rain.”

name: Gabbai
dictNote: (tax gatherer), apparently the head of an important family of Benjamin resident at Jerusalem. (Nehemiah 11:8) (B.C. before 536.)

name: Shamsherai
dictNote: (sunlike), a Benjamite. (1 Chronicles 8:26)

name: Tophel
note: Tophel, a place near the Desert
dictNote: Lime, a place in the wilderness of Sinai (Deut. 1:1), now identified with Tafyleh or Tufileh, on the west side of the Edomitish mountains.

name: Ahiramites
note: an Achiramite or descendant (collectively) of Achiram

name: Dehavites
note: Dahava, a people colonized in Samaria
dictNote: Villagers, one of the Assyrian tribes which Asnapper sent to repopulate Samaria (Ezra 4:9). They were probably a nomad Persian tribe on the east of the Caspian Sea, and near the Sea of Azof.

name: Arab
dictNote: Ambush, a city in the mountains of Judah (Josh. 15:52), now Er-Rabiyeh.

name: Ben-hail

Others identify it with Sardis, the capital of Lydia. The Latin father Jerome regarded it as an Assyrian word, meaning “boundary,” and interpreted the sentence, “which is in Sepharad,” by “who are scattered abroad in all the boundaries and regions of the earth.” Perowne says: “Whatever uncertainty attaches to the word Sepharad, the drift of the prophecy is clear, viz., that not only the exiles from Babylon, but Jewish captives from other and distant regions, shall be brought back to live prosperously within the enlarged borders of their own land.”

name: Sargon
dictNote: (In the inscriptions, “Sarra-yukin” [the god] has appointed the king; also “Sarru-kinu,” the legitimate king.) On the death of Shalmaneser (B.C. 723), one of the Assyrian generals established himself on the vacant throne, taking the name of “Sargon,” after that of the famous monarch, the Sargon of Accad, founder of the first Semitic empire, as well as of one of the most famous libraries of Chaldea. He forthwith began a conquering career, and became one of the most powerful of the Assyrian monarchs. He is mentioned by name in the Bible only in connection with the siege of Ashdod (Isa. 20:1). At the very beginning of his reign he besieged and took the city of Samaria (2 Kings 17:6; 18:9-12). On an inscription found in the palace he built at Khorsabad, near Nieveh, he says, “The city of Samaria I besieged, I took; 27,280 of its inhabitants I carried away; fifty chariots that were among them I collected,” etc. The northern kingdom he changed into an Assyrian satrapy. He afterwards drove Merodach-baladan (q.v.), who kept him at bay for twelve years, out of Babylon, which he entered in triumph. By a succession of victories he gradually enlarged and consolidated the empire, which now extended from the frontiers of Egypt in the west to the mountains of Elam in the east, and thus carried almost to completion the ambitious designs of Tiglath-pileser (q.v.). He was murdered by one of his own soldiers (B.C. 705) in his palace at Khorsabad, after a reign of sixteen years, and was succeeded by his son Sennacherib.

dictNote: Nahum was a prophet whose short book announces the coming destruction of Nineveh, the Assyrian capital that had once repented under Jonah's preaching but had since returned to its cruelty, and Nahum describes Nineveh's fall in vivid, almost gleeful detail as deserved judgment for the empire's brutality toward the nations it conquered.

name: Areopagite
note: an Areopagite or member of the court held on Mars' Hill
dictNote: A member of the court of Areopagus (Acts 17:34).

name: Perazim
dictNote: (a breach), Mount, a name which occurs in (Isaiah 28:21) only—unless the place which it designates is identical with the Baal-perazim mentioned as the scene of one of David’s victories over the Philistines, which was in the valley of Rephaim, south of Jerusalem, on the road to Bethlehem.

name: Zamzummim
note: a Zamzumite, or native tribe of Palestine
dictNote: The Zamzummim were a people of great size and numbers whom the Lord destroyed before the Ammonites so that Ammon could settle their territory east of the Jordan, an episode Moses recalls as evidence that God had cleared land for other nations besides Israel (Deuteronomy 2:20-21). Some identify them with the Zuzim, a similarly obscure people defeated earlier by the coalition of eastern kings in Genesis 14.

name: Chloe
dictNote: Verdure, a female Christian (1 Cor. 1:11), some of whose household had informed Paul of the divided state of the Corinthian church. Nothing is known of her.

name: Ben-ammi
dictNote: Son of my kindred; i.e., “born of incest”, the son of Lot by his youngest daughter (Gen. 19:38).

name: Cosam
dictNote: (a diviner), son of Elmodam, in the line of Joseph the husband of Mary. (Luke 3:28)

name: Zareth-shahar
dictNote: The splendour of the dawn, a city “in the mount of the valley” (Josh. 13:19). It is identified with the ruins of Zara, near the mouth of the Wady Zerka Main, on the eastern shore of the Dead Sea, some 3 miles south of the Callirrhoe. Of this town but little remains. “A few broken basaltic columns and pieces of wall about 200 yards back from the shore, and a ruined fort rather nearer the sea, about the middle of the coast line of the plain, are all that are left” (Tristram’s Land of Moab).

name: Nibhaz
note: Nibchaz, a deity of the Avites
dictNote: Barker, the name of an idol, supposed to be an evil demon of the Zabians. It was set up in Samaria by the Avites (2 Kings 17:31), probably in the form of a dog.

name: Bar-jona
note: son of Jonas (or Jonah); Bar-jonas, an Israelite
dictNote: Son of Jonah, the patronymic of Peter (Matt. 16:17; John 1:42), because his father’s name was Jonas. (See PETER.)

name: Iscah
dictNote: Spy, the daughter of Haran and sister of Milcah and Lot (Gen. 11:29, 31).

name: Jaziz
dictNote: (whom God moves), a Hagarite who had charge of the flocks of King David. (1 Chronicles 27:31) (B.C. 1046.)

name: Shicron
note: drunkenness, Shikkeron, a place in Palestine
dictNote: (drunkenness), one of the landmarks at the western end of the north boundary of Judah. (Joshua 15:11) only. It lay between Ekron (Akir) and Jabneel (Yebna).

name: Hadar
dictNote: Adod, brave(?). (1.) A son of Ishmael (Gen. 25:15); in 1 Chr. 1:30 written Hadad. (2.) One of the Edomitish kings (Gen. 36:39) about the time of Saul. Called also Hadad (1 Chr. 1:50, 51). It is probable that in these cases Hadar may be an error simply of transcription for Hadad.

name: Jesher
dictNote: Uprightness, the first of the three sons of Caleb by Azubah (1 Chr. 2:18).

name: Hakkatan
dictNote: (young). Johanan son of Hakkatan, was the chief of the Bene-Azgad who returned from Babylon with Ezra. (Ezra 8:12)

Greece was conquered by the Romans B.C. 146. After passing through various changes it was erected into an independent monarchy in 1831. name: Miphkad

name: Addi
dictNote: Ornament, (Luke 3:28), the son of Cosam, and father of Melchi, one of the progenitors of Christ.

name: Bosor

secondTemple.excerpt: To this exhortation Judas hearkened, and returned to the wilderness; and in the first place fell upon the inhabitants of Bosor, and took the city, and beat the inhabitants, and destroyed all the males, and all that were able to fight, and burnt the city.

dictNote: The Chaldee or Aramaic form of the name Beor, the father of Balaam (2 Pet. 2:15).

name: Obal
dictNote: Stripped, the eight son of Joktan (Gen. 10:28); called also Ebal (1 Chr. 1:22).

name: Baal-hazor
dictNote: Having a courtyard, or Baal’s village, the place on the borders of Ephraim and Benjamin where Absalom held the feast of sheep-shearing when Amnon was assassinated (2 Sam. 13:23). Probably it is the same with Hazor (Neh. 11:33), now Tell’ Asur, 5 miles north-east of Bethel.

name: Hamuel
dictNote: (heat, i.e. wrath, of God), a man of Simeon, of the family of Shaul. (1 Chronicles 4:26)

name: Zephath
dictNote: Beacon; watch-tower, a Canaanite town; called also Hormah (q.v.), Judg. 1:17. It has been identified with the pass of es-Sufah, but with greater probability with S’beita.

name: Zuriel
dictNote: Rock of God, chief of the family of the Merarites (Num. 3:35) at the time of the Exodus.

name: Mahol

dictNote: Dance, the father of four sons (1 Kings 4:31) who were inferior in wisdom only to Solomon.

name: Hezion
dictNote: Vision, the father of Tabrimon, and grandfather of Ben-hadad, king of Syria (1 Kings 15:18).

placePhoto.description: panorama of a plain in Beth-eden

name: Dimnah
dictNote: Dunghill, a city of Zebulun given to the Merarite Levites (Josh. 21:35). In 1 Chr. 6:77 the name “Rimmon” is substituted.

name: Ohel
dictNote: A house; tent, the fourth son of Zerubbabel (1 Chr. 3:20).

name: Phalec
dictNote: (Luke 3:35)=Peleg (q.v.), Gen. 11:16.

name: Regem
dictNote: (friend) a son of Jahdai. (1 Chronicles 2:47)

name: Peulthai
dictNote: Wages of the Lord, one of the sons of Obed-edom, a Levite porter (1 Chr. 26:5).

name: Temeni
dictNote: One of the sons of Ashur, the father of Tekoa (1 Chr. 4:6).

name: Vophsi
dictNote: (rich), father of Nahbi, the Naphtalite spy. (Numbers 13:14) (B.C. before 1490.)

name: Beth-barah
dictNote: House of crossing, a place south of the scene of Gideon’s victory (Judg. 7:24). It was probably the chief ford of the Jordan in that district, and may have been that by which Jacob crossed when he returned from Mesopotamia, near the Jabbok (Gen. 32:22), and at which Jephthah slew the Ephraimites (Judg. 12:4). Nothing, however, is certainly known of it. (See BETHABARA.)

name: Beth-rehob
dictNote: (house of Rehob), place mentioned as having near it the valley in which lay the town of Laish or Dan. (Judges 18:28) It was one of the little kingdoms of Aram or Syria. (2 Samuel 10:6) Robinson conjectures that this ancient place is represented by the modern Hunin .

name: Ahuzam
dictNote: (possession), properly Ahuzzam son of Ashur, the father or founder of Tekoa, by his wife Naarah. (1 Chronicles 4:6)

name: Hazaiah
dictNote: (whom Jehovah sees), a man of Judah of the family of the Shilonites, or descendants of Shelah. (Nehemiah 11:5)

name: Bariah
dictNote: Fugitive, one of Shemaiah’s five sons. Their father is counted along with them in 1 Chr. 3:22.

name: Ezel
note: Ezel, a memorial stone in Palestine
dictNote: A separation, (1 Sam. 20:19), a stone, or heap of stones, in the neighbourhood of Saul’s residence, the scene of the parting of David and Jonathan (42). The margin of the Authorized Version reads, “The stone that sheweth the way,” in this rendering following the Targum.

name: Lecah
dictNote: (progress), a name mentioned in the genealogies of Judah, (1 Chronicles 4:21) only, as one of the descendants of Shelah, the third son of Judah by the Canaanites Bath-shua.

name: Bithiah
dictNote: (daughter of the Lord), daughter of a Pharaoh, and wife of Mered. (1 Chronicles 4:18) (B.C. about 1491.)

name: Mispereth
dictNote: one of those who returned with Zerubbabel and Jeshua from Babylon. (Nehemiah 7:7)

name: Beth-pazzez
dictNote: (house of the dispersion), a town of Issachar named with En-haddah (Joshua 19:21) and of which nothing is known.

name: Zaham
dictNote: (fatness), son of Rehoboam by Abihail the daughter of Eliab. (2 Chronicles 11:19)

name: Iru
dictNote: (watch), the eldest son of the great Caleb son of Jephunneh. (1 Chronicles 4:15) (B.C. 1451.)

name: Haphraim
dictNote: (two pits), a city of Issachar, mentioned next to Shunem. (Joshua 19:19) About 6 miles northeast of Lejjun, and two miles west of Solam (the ancient Shunem), stands the village of el’ Afuleh, which may possibly be the representative of Haphraim.

name: Eliphal
dictNote: (whom God judges), son of Ur, one of David’s guard. (1 Chronicles 11:35) [Eliphelet, 3]

name: Jezerite
note: an Iezrite or descendant of Iezer

name: Jahdo
dictNote: (united), a Gadite, (1 Chronicles 5:14) son of Buz and father of Jeshishai.

name: Jogli
dictNote: (led into exile), the father of Bukki, a Danite chief. (Numbers 34:22)

name: Stachys
dictNote: Spike; an ear of corn, a convert at Rome whom Paul salutes (Rom. 16:9).

name: Chisloth-tabor
dictNote: (loins of Tabor) a place to the border of which reached the border of Zebulun. (Joshua 19:12) It may be the village Iksal, which is now standing about 2 1/2 miles to the west of Mount Tabor.

name: Gedeon
dictNote: The Greek form of the Hebrew name Gideon. (Hebrews 11:32)

name: Shinab
dictNote: Cooling, the king of Adamah, in the valley of Siddim, who with his confederates was conquered by Chedorlaomer (Gen. 14:2).

name: Shuphamite
note: a Shuphamite (collectively) or descendants of Shephupham

name: Baal-tamar
dictNote: Lord of palm trees, a place in the tribe of Benjamin near Gibeah of Saul (Judg. 20:33). It was one of the sanctuaries or groves of Baal. Probably the palm tree of Deborah (Judg. 4:5) is alluded to in the name.

name: Makaz
dictNote: (end), a place, apparently a town, named once only— (1 Kings 4:9)—in the: specification of the jurisdiction of Solomon a commissariat officer, Ben-Dekar. Makaz has not been discovered.

name: Methuselah
note: Luke names him only as a link in the chain, ‘son of Methuselah’ — but the Book of Noah fragment gives him an actual scene: the grandfather who travels to find Enoch when his newborn grandson's birth looks less than human.

dictNote: Man of the dart, the son of Enoch, and grandfather of Noah. He was the oldest man of whom we have any record, dying at the age of nine hundred and sixty-nine years, in the year of the Flood (Gen. 5:21-27; 1 Chr. 1:3).

name: Shiza
dictNote: (splendor), a Reubenite, father of Adina, (1 Chronicles 11:42) one of David’s warriors. (B.C. 1043.)

name: Shemidaites
note: a Shemidaite (collectively) or descendants of Shemida

name: Quartus
dictNote: Fourth, a Corinthian Christian who sent by Paul his salutations to friends at Rome (Rom. 16:23).

name: Hadrach
dictNote: The name of a country (Zech. 9:1) which cannot be identified. Rawlinson would identify it with Edessa. name: Ben
dictNote: (son), a Levite, one of the porters appointed by David for the ark. (1 Chronicles 15:18)

name: Belial
note: worthlessness; Belial, as an epithet of Satan
dictNote: Worthlessness, frequently used in the Old Testament as a proper name. It is first used in Deut. 13:13. It is translated “wicked” in Deut. 15:9; Ps. 41:8 (R.V. marg.); 101:3; Prov. 6:12, etc. The expression “son” or “man of Belial” means simply a worthless, lawless person (Judg. 19:22; 20:13; 1 Sam. 1:16; 2:12).

name: Saraph
dictNote: (burning) mentioned in (1 Chronicles 4:22) among the descendants of Judah.

name: Emmor
dictNote: An ass, Acts 7:16. (See HAMOR.)

name: Artemas
note: gift of Artemis; Artemas (or Artemidorus), a Christian
dictNote: (gift of Artemis), a companion of St. Paul. (Titus 3:12) According to tradition he was bishop of Lystra.

name: Hoshama
dictNote: (whom Jehovah hears), one of the sons of Jeconiah or Jehoiachin, the last king but one of Judah. (1 Chronicles 3:18)

name: Beeroth of the children of Jaakan
note: Beeroth-Bene-Jaakan, a place in the Desert
dictNote: (Deut. 10:6). The same as Bene-jaakan (Num. 33:31).

name: Pethuel
dictNote: Vision of God, the father of Joel the prophet (Joel 1:1).

name: Ardites

dictNote: the descendants of Ard or Addar, the grandson of Benjamin. (Numbers 26:40)

name: Elishaphat
dictNote: Whom God has judged, one of the “captains of hundreds” associated with Jehoiada in the league to overthrow the usurpation of Athaliah (2 Chr. 23:1).

name: En-eglaim
dictNote: Fountain of two calves, a place mentioned only in Ezek. 47:10. Somewhere near the Dead Sea.

name: Ir
dictNote: (city). (1 Chronicles 7:12) [Iri]

name: Kitron
dictNote: Knotty, a city of Zebulun (Judg. 1:30), called also Kattath (Josh. 19:15); supposed to be “Cana of Galilee.”

name: Shemeber

name: Asiel
dictNote: (created by God).

name: Zenas
dictNote: A disciple called “the lawyer,” whom Paul wished Titus to bring with him (Titus 3:13). Nothing more is known of him.

name: Ithnan
dictNote: (given), one of the towns in the extreme south of Judah. (Joshua 15:23) No trace of its existence has yet been discovered.

name: Jidlaph
dictNote: (weeping), a son of Nahor. (Genesis 22:22)

name: Meroz
dictNote: A plain in the north of Palestine, the inhabitants of which were severely condemned because they came not to help Barak against Sisera (Judg. 5:23: comp. 21:8-10; 1 Sam. 11:7). dictNote: A hill or hill-town, “of Benjamin” (1 Sam. 13:15), better known as “Gibeah of Saul” (11:4; Isa. 10:29). It was here that the terrible outrage was committed on the Levite’s concubine which led to the almost utter extirpation of the tribe of Benjamin (Judg. 19; 20), only six hundred men surviving after a succession of disastrous battles. This was the birthplace of Saul, and continued to be his residence after he became king (1 Sam. 10:26; 11:4; 15:34). It was reckoned among the ancient sanctuaries of Palestine (10:26; 15:34; 23:19; 26:1; 2 Sam. 21:6-10), and hence it is called “Gibeah of God” (1 Sam. 10:5, R.V. marg.). He beheaded John the Baptist (Matt. 14:1-12) at the instigation of Herodias, the wife of his half-brother Herod-Philip, whom he had married. name: Accad
dictNote: The high land or mountains, a city in the land of Shinar. It has been identified with the mounds of Akker Kuf, some 50 miles to the north of Babylon; but this is doubtful. It was one of the cities of Nimrod’s kingdom (Ge 10:10). It stood close to the Euphrates, opposite Sippara. (See SEPHARVAIM.) It is also the name of the country of which this city was the capital, namely, northern or upper Babylonia. The Accadians who came from the “mountains of the east,” where the ark rested, attained to a high degree of civilization. In the Babylonian inscriptions they are called “the black heads” and “the black faces,” in contrast to “the white race” of Semitic descent. They invented the form of writing in pictorial hieroglyphics, and also the cuneiform system, in which they wrote many books partly on papyrus and partly on clay. The Semitic Babylonians (“the white race”), or, as some scholars think, first the Cushites, and afterwards, as a second immigration, the Semites, invaded and conquered this country; and then the Accadian language ceased to be a spoken language, although for the sake of its literary treasures it continued to be studied by the educated classes of Babylonia. A large portion of the Ninevite tablets brought to light by Oriental research consists of interlinear or parallel translations from Accadian into Assyrian; and thus that long-forgotten language has been recovered by scholars. It belongs to the class of languages called agglutinative, common to the Tauranian race; i.e., it consists of words “glued together,” without declension of conjugation. These tablets in a remarkable manner illustrate ancient history. Among other notable records, they contain an account of the Creation which closely resembles that given in the book of Genesis, of the Sabbath as a day of rest, and of the Deluge and its cause. (See BABYLON; CHALDEA.)

He made war against Hoshea, the king of Israel, whom he subdued and compelled to pay an annual tribute. Hoshea, however, soon after rebelled against his Assyrian conquerer. Shalmaneser again marched against Samaria, which, after a siege of three years, was taken (2 Kings 17:3-5; 18:9) by Sargon (q.v.). A revolution meantime had broken out in Assyria, and Shalmaneser was deposed. Sargon usurped the vacant throne.
